Principle 4 (One Selection, Five Projections): switching views changes projection rather than place, resolving the selected target in the destination view and pulsing Strand's 150 ms amber continuity halo.

Principle 5 (Quarantine Without Hostage-Taking): untrusted macros, missing external links and heavy recalc queues open immediately in safe cached state behind clear Mast quarantine pills instead of blocking modal startup dialogs.

Cold start (≤65 ms) opens a calm Start Stage on mist paper with no tour popups or account wall, offering Open Workbook (Ctrl+O / drag-and-drop), New Blank Workbook (Ctrl+N), Open Formula Explorer (Ctrl+Shift+E), and a 4-line Excel Power-User Note.

First open of Inherited.xlsm (M-01): snaps petrol shell at 55 ms and paints cached values of active sheet at 190 ms while streaming background dependency indexing (Strip 74% -> 100% at 1,180 ms); replaces Excel's blocking dialogs with a keyboard-reachable Quarantine Bar (Alt+Q: Macros Blocked Module1, 2 Missing Links Held at cached values) and auto-Triage Strip linking to Inspector; Bridge shows inline upstream root-error cell under the Formula Bar; Sheet Drawer [≡ 40 Sheets] reveals sheet formula counts and [+9 Hidden] including VeryHidden; polite screen-reader announcement summarizes file state.
why: Eliminates modal startup walls while keeping stale/external/error state transparent.
evidence: M-01; Inherited.xlsm (40 sheets, 304,812 fmls, 417 errors / 3 roots)

statement: Inspector view on Inherited.xlsm (Ctrl+2, 95 ms, M-02) preserves Mast/Bridge/Strip and pulses a 140 ms amber continuity halo; folds 417 error cells into 3 topological roots (including automatic string near-match diagnosis for trailing-space VLOOKUP #N/A), draws missing external links as ◈ boundary nodes with cached timestamps, summarises dense 248k-formula sheets at block level, flags volatile OFFSET fan-out (6 names dirtying 184k cells, 412 ms recalc cost), and discloses Hidden and xlSheetVeryHidden sheets plus dead zero-dependent backup sheets.
why: Gives immediate structural X-ray of huge legacy workbooks in one view.

statement: Keyboard navigation from Inspector ROOT ERRORS (Tab, Enter, Ctrl+1) jumps to Classic centered on Gas_Daily_2001!AT142 in 11 ms via virtualised grid rendering; hovering AS142 shows a 1-line readout, and Ctrl++ semantic zoom (150%) scales tabular numerals crisply without mutating the file.
Toggling Formula Lens (Alt+L) in Classic displays a dual-line readable translation synthesized from row/column headers and defined names above the unchanged raw Excel formula.

First switch to Notebook (Ctrl+3, 85 ms) auto-arranges an initial outline from workbook structure (Assumptions scenario parameter card, FY27 Executive Summary pulsing amber continuity halo on active cell, Monthly Operating Pipeline Data Frame with frozen stub and sparklines) while stating that cells remain unchanged in Excel.

Notebook write-up (M-03) uses Source Serif 4 (Reading density, 68 ch) for prose with '@' inline live reference chips (rounded 5 px tokens) and inline scenario controls (Inputs!C2); toggling Downside sweeps an amber dependency ripple in 6 ms updating Data Frame, KPIs and prose chips synchronously (Pluto-style reactivity); folded assumptions disclose exact count ('+9 remaining'); Ctrl+Z reverts across Notebook and Classic; prose and layout persist safely in xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml.
why: Eliminates stale copy-pasted memos while preserving 100% native Excel workbooks.

statement: Copying Notebook prose and tables writes rich HTML + plain Markdown with evaluated formatted numbers for external email/doc apps, while pasting inside DNA Calc preserves live cell references.

Selecting two disagreeing numeric cells (Ctrl+Click) displays their delta and '[Trace Discrepancy (Ctrl+2)]' in the Strip and opens Inspector's Dual-Path Comparison & Discrepancy Waterfall (M-04, 28 ms over 25k rows): visualizes partial table coverage (88.0% clip seam skipping 3,001 rows worth +$198,450), catches trailing-space dirty criteria keys ('West␣' at Orders!C23804 worth +$37,000), accounts for 100% of the -$235,450 gap ($0 residual), offers a Ghost Preview fix rewriting C5:C8 to structured Orders[Col] refs, and flags clipped ranges as a non-red warning.
why: Reconciles silent formula-vs-pivot discrepancies where Excel shows zero errors.

statement: Docked Formula Explorer (Ctrl+Shift+E) verifies predicate filter match counts, previews the structured-reference fix before Enter, jumps straight to the dirty cell in Classic (Ctrl+1) to strip trailing whitespace (9 ms recalc with green fresh tick ✓), supports 2-step Ctrl+Z undo, and exports the Discrepancy Card to clipboard (Ctrl+Shift+C).

Empty Model Map (18 ms) offers keyboard-first creation (G for prefix group, N for named block, Tab for connected sibling) backed by plain Excel cells and workbook-scoped defined names on the sheet, using the AST Formula-Name Presenter & Interpreter to resolve short local names inside groups.

Closing a circular feedback loop when Excel Iterative Calculation is OFF pauses the wire in an inline Preview Seam offering [1] Enable Ticks Director (Iter=ON, Max=1, Δ=0.001), [2] Enable Equilibrium Iteration (Max=100, Δ=0.001), or [Esc] Cancel wire; committing renders a double-line teal-600 [z⁻¹] arc and Director bar; right-clicking a parameter attaches a genuine OOXML Form Control ScrollBar rendered right inside the actor card.

Stock.xlsx on Model Map (M-05) shows Director bar (Ticks Iter=1, ▶ Run, Step F9, Reset, t=14), [z⁻¹] self-reference feedback arcs, 140 ms amber topological firing pulse on F9 step, embedded OOXML Form Control slider for Policy.ReorderPoint, live 3-element dynamic-array spill {0, 0, 400} inside Supply.DelayPipe, and honest Strip readout of iteration settings and deliberate loops.

Checking map-authored Stock.xlsx in Classic (Ctrl+1, M-06) reveals cleanly allocated label/value rows grouped by prefix, defined-name priority in the Address Box with linked-control metadata, 120 fps Form Control ScrollBar syncing with constant styling, teal-ink [↻] iterative cell badges, and teal-600 dynamic-array spill outline around C11:E11.

Opening a workbook with preferredView='app' lands in App View in 75 ms with Bridge collapsed to [Show Formulas (Alt+L)]; formula outcome cards are write-protected against literal clobbering and respond to typing with a polite inline callout offering Goal Seek ('Solve Principal for $2,400/mo…') instead of overwriting formulas.

App scenario comparison and printing (M-07): '[Pin Current as Baseline]' freezes reference values so input tweaks recalculate 360 rows in 3 ms showing live directional deltas (▼ -$154,652.46, -91 months) with screen-reader announcements, non-mutating annual rollup toggle over 360 monthly rows, and a Ctrl+P Executive 2-Page Print Drawer always rendered in cockpit-light daylight paper with explicit opt-in checkbox for the full 360-row table (+6 pages).

Standalone DNA Calc - Formula Explorer (M-08) cold-launches in 35 ms with dot-long [•━] mark and zero workbook chrome into a 3-pane workbench (Synthetic Inputs Shelf + XLL library, Formula & Live AST Tree with dual IEEE-754 raw + formatted readout and timing, Number/Conditional Format testers + Auto Boundary Probe Matrix); shadow-copies local .xll files on load behind a Developer Sandbox Strip so add-in devs recompile without DLL locks and hot-reload in 45 ms via Ctrl+Shift+R.

Using an add-in UDF in Classic (M-09) displays notched reference tokens (①②③), live mid-edit evaluated preview and Excel-safe cache portability note before Enter, matching on-sheet notched frames, cross-sheet precedent badges on sheet tabs (Inputs [①③]), and ◈ add-in provenance glyph.

AI Agent Staged Change-Set (M-10, Ctrl+J): never overwrites cells directly; groups R1C1-equivalent edits into logical hunks overlaid in hatched ghost preview, computes cross-sheet KPI output impact across scenarios upfront (catching unintended Base EBITDA +$265k leak from Hunk 3), supports keyboard review (J/K navigate, A accept, R reject with optional agent reply), discards cleanly on Esc, and commits only accepted hunks on Enter.

Granular Agent Undo & Provenance Stack (Ctrl+Shift+Z, M-11): multi-hunk agent commits push per-hunk atomic entries under a collapsible Agent group so a single Ctrl+Z reverts only Hunk 2 while preserving Hunk 1 and keeping Hunk 2 on Ctrl+Y redo, with prompt and hunk counts logged in optional customXml session provenance.

Make-or-break coverage table maps all eleven UX verification categories (first run, discovery, loading/calc feedback, view switching, refusals, undo, copy/paste, hover/focus, perceived speed, accessibility, Excel-user wins) to exact Section 2 storyboards.
All five views project one shared Excel workbook graph using one canonical Target Address grammar shared identically by humans (Ctrl+G/Ctrl+K) and AI agents.

Seven-level unified Target Address hierarchy: (1) Cell (Monthly!O20), (2) Range/Dynamic Spill (Monthly!C11:N11, C11#), (3) Inferred Block (#Monthly.OpEx), (4) Defined Name (Stock.OnHand, LAMBDA/OFFSET), (5) Table/Pivot (Orders[NetAmount], Pivot_RegionSKU), (6) Sheet Object (Chart_Amortisation, ScrollBar1), and (7) Presentation-only View Item (@notebook/sec-1/prose-1, @app/card-interest) stored in xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml.

Cross-view focus is tracked as (ActiveModelTarget, OptionalViewItem): switching views (Ctrl+1..5) resolves ActiveModelTarget to its tightest visible projection within 100 ms with a 150 ms amber continuity halo (0 ms under reduced motion), and switching from a pure Notebook prose View Item lands on the nearest referenced cell/chip or following Data Frame anchor.

Non-grid edit semantics under 1-bit SELECTED/EDITING and Backing-Sheet Primacy: scalar controls write directly to bound cells; Model Map/Notebook formulas run through the bidirectional AST Presenter/Interpreter; editing a Notebook 12-month formula run previews all 12 R1C1-identical cells (Shift+Enter for single cell) and refuses silent clobbering of overrides; Delete clears cells in Classic, removes only presentation cards [V] in Notebook/App, and prompts Map-only vs Delete-backing-cell (Shift+Delete) with blast-radius preview on Model Map.

One chronological Workbook Undo/Redo stack (Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, inspectable via Ctrl+Shift+Z) spans all views and docked Explorer with [M] Model and [V] View badges; Ctrl+Z undoes the last action regardless of active view without yanking viewport (showing a Strip confirmation with [Jump]), while pure navigation, tree folding and Explorer sandbox tests never pollute Undo.

Unified semantic state signaling across all views: Evaluation errors (red #D02A23 border + [!] + Bridge root subtitle, bubbling to parent blocks), Active focus/calc (amber #FFB301 + 140 ms topological ripple), Stale manual-calc values (desaturated hatched [stale] corner + amber Strip [F9 Recalc Needed]), External/volatile/live (signal orange #FF8001 + ◈ + optional Events Queue), and Calculation Directors (Recalc, Manual, Iteration, Ticks, Sweep, Events).

Agent four-stage lifecycle: Stage tool calls into an isolated copy-on-write Staged Change-Set (Δ Agent #N), collapse R1C1-identical diffs into sage-400 hatched Hunks with cross-scenario KPI blast-radius diff, review via J/K/E/A/R/Ctrl+Enter/Esc, and commit accepted hunks as hunk-atomic [M] Undo entries under a collapsible Agent #N provenance group.
All five views share the One Shell, honour Formula Lens (Alt+L), and switch in <100 ms via Ctrl+1..Ctrl+5 or Ctrl+K; touch and pen are deferred for v1 with explicit hook points noted per view.

Classic (Ctrl+1) is the default view for unannotated workbooks with 100% Appendix A keyboard/mouse parity, notched ①②③④ cross-sheet range picking, future inertial two-finger pan / stylus tap-to-pick hooks, best fit for tabular authoring/virtualised grids, and complemented by Inspector/Notebook/Map/App for triage, prose, feedback loops and consumer apps.

Classic full-screen reference (M-12): single-line 30 px Command Strip accepting Alt chords (e.g., Alt, H, V, S), Formula Bar with notched tokens [①C7] and [②Inputs!$C$8] plus live Lens preview, subtle constant provenance marker (c / prov-const), matching notched grid highlights, off-sheet scalar peek on sheet tabs (Inputs [② $420]), and explicit POINT mode Strip readout.

Inspector (Ctrl+2 or Strip error pill) is a Phyphox-inspired multi-probe diagnostic bench: Up/Down walks roots/bottlenecks, Left/Right steps precedents/dependents, Space peeks backing slice inline, Ctrl+Click compares two targets, F9 profiles per-stage milliseconds, Enter jumps to Classic.

Inspector full-screen reference (M-13): combines Active Probe Header, Phyphox-style topological Calculation Chain Cost Meter (identifying Gas_Daily_2001 as 88% / 364 ms of recalc), Root-Cause & Structural Hygiene Scanner (47 hardcoded overrides inside formula columns, OFFSET blast radius, hidden/VeryHidden sheets), Live/External/Macro Inventory, and a zero-switch 5-row Inline Cell Peek at bottom.

Notebook (Ctrl+3) provides Pluto-style live reactive documents backed 100% by Excel in ↓ Page or → Pipeline flow; Up/Down moves blocks, Enter edits prose/Data Frame, @ inserts live cell chips, / opens block-insert menu, Alt+L toggles Lens rules; auto-synthesises Inputs→Calculations→Summaries on first visit and declines full inline expansion of 285k-cell legacy sheets.

Notebook Horizontal Pipeline reference (M-14): arranges Inputs → Monthly Engine → FY27 KPIs left-to-right connected by real precedent flow connectors, with reactive prose header, live add-in values (FK.SAAS_LTV), and inline native workbook charts.

Model map (Ctrl+4) renders hierarchical actor-and-wire schematics with Directors (Recalc, Ticks, Iteration, Sweep, Events), [z⁻¹] delays and IFS/SWITCH state diagrams; Arrows traverse wires, Enter drills in / Alt+Up climbs breadcrumb, F2 edits via short-name Interpreter, N/Tab create blocks, port dragging rewrites formulas with Preview Seam, Ctrl+Wheel executes semantic zoom (text ≥11 px); collapses 360-row schedules to one composite and refuses 248k-cell explosions.

Model Map full-screen reference (M-15): shows bidirectional Presenter for =IFS(...) guards, breadcrumb + Ticks Director bar, live 3-state pill diagram inside IFS modal blocks ((Normal)→(•Reorder*)→(Stockout)), embedded Form Control slider, and dockable transient History Strip plotting tick trajectories without writing history arrays into the .xlsx.

App view (Ctrl+5 or preferredView='app') provides accessible web-app ergonomics (Tab across unlocked inputs only, arrows step sliders, Pin Baseline, Ctrl+Shift+A Edit App Layout for builders, 40 px future touch targets) and declines auto-synthesis on messy unannotated workbooks like Inherited.

App full-screen reference (M-16): collapsed formula bar with baseline pin and Reset Inputs, protected outcome cards using semantic delta arrows (▼/▲ + ✓), dual-curve chart overlaying dotted baseline vs solid current scenario, and annual rollup toggle over 360 monthly rows.

Formula Explorer ships in two forms sharing one workbench: Form A docked inside a workbook (Ctrl+Shift+E) with non-destructive Sandbox Try overrides until Ctrl+Enter apply, and Form B standalone stripped build (35 ms launch, [•━] mark, synthetic fixtures, .xll hot-reload, .dnafe.json snippets); clicking/arrowing any AST node highlights its substring and shows intermediate value, type, and microseconds.

Docked in-workbook Formula Explorer reference (M-17): keeps the spilled cell visible above while showing seeded workbook inputs with Sandbox Try override ($50k -> $75k shrinking FILTER from 8 to 2 rows without touching sheet), live AST values, multi-state number format preview, and spill-aware conditional formatting rule match counts.

Standalone Formula Explorer full-screen reference (M-18): [•━] zero-workbook chrome, multi-line LET/LAMBDA formatter (Shift+Alt+F) with line numbers, fixture bindings + presets, simultaneous intermediate LET variable readouts, 1×3 spilled output card, combined format + conditional rule check, and standalone engine Strip (512 built-in functions).

Formula Lens (Alt+L in every view) never mutates stored formulas and offers three presentation layers: (1) readable reference substitution from defined/inferred names with raw Excel below, (2) prefix stripping in scoped group contexts, and (3) read-only virtual LET de-duplication of repeated sub-expressions (rewriting the cell only if the user clicks [Refactor Cell to LET]).

Background structural recognition analyses formula ASTs, R1C1 equivalence classes, spatial adjacency, header typography, OOXML metadata and precedent graphs so views work out of the box while allowing user correction.

Three calibrated pattern confidence tiers: Deterministic (100%: native OOXML Tables, Pivots, Form Controls, Data Tables, RTD/external, VBA, iterative loops), High Confidence (≥85%: AST + layout convergence used for auto-synthesis), and Probable/Ambiguous (50–84%: keeps raw coordinates beside a dashed '[? Confirm ✓ | Split | Rename]' chip).

Users and agents confirm or correct inferred blocks via right-click or Ctrl+Shift+B (Confirm, Rename, Merge/Split, Re-tag role, Mark Override as Intentional), persisted purely in xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml without touching Excel cells.

Carbon organises 19 recurring patterns (15 core + 4 essential additions: #16 Reconciliation & check blocks, #17 Ragged hierarchies & SUBTOTAL/AGGREGATE rollups, #18 Dynamic array spill pipelines & LAMBDA helpers, #19 Override & manual-adjustment layers) into five structural families mapped across all five views in Appendix D.
why: Covers corporate audit hazards (double-counted subtotals, silent overrides, tie-out checks) and modern dynamic arrays.

statement: Inherited.xlsm (40 sheets, 9 hidden, 304,812 formulas, Gas_Daily_2001 A1:CV2850, missing links, macros, 6 volatile OFFSET names, 417 errors) defines the big-workbook stress benchmark.

Classic at scale: always 100% virtualised (~60×25 visible cells mounted), never declines any legal Excel sheet, switches to Semantic Minimap LOD below 70% zoom, and collapses >12 tabs into searchable [≡ 40 Sheets] drawer.

Inspector at scale: shows full block graph for ≤2,000 formulas/≤10 sheets; above that folds errors to roots, collapses R1C1 runs, groups 40 sheet clusters, samples value distributions >50k rows with exact recompute option, and declines >2,500-edge cell hairballs while offering 2-hop expansion.

Notebook at scale: renders ≤15 blocks and ≤200-row tables inline; windows larger tables to 15 rows + sticky totals and pins first/last periods + sparkline for >12 periods; declines auto-generating prose for >25,000-formula unannotated dense sheets with options to pin ranges or open Inspector.

Model map at scale: shows ≤80 blocks directly; groups 81–1,500 blocks into drillable Composite Districts, bundles parallel wires with edge counts and bubbled errors; declines flat diagrams >500 distinct R1C1 blocks in favor of column-zone districts or 2-hop neighbourhood mapping.

App at scale: works with explicit App specs or ≤25 clear inputs + outputs; collapses detail tables behind KPIs/rollups; declines auto-guessing on messy error-ridden workbooks (>50 scattered constants, 417 errors) offering manual range selection or Inspector triage.
Budget: cold shell ready ≤80 ms desktop (≤150 ms warm WASM browser).
Budget: Inherited (18.4 MB) open to interactive cached first paint ≤250 ms with zero main-thread stalls >16 ms.
Budget: off-thread dependency & R1C1 block indexing of 304,812 formulas ≤1,500 ms with live Strip progress and uninterrupted navigation.
Budget: keystroke/cursor/scroll ≤16 ms p95 (≤25 ms p99, 60–120 fps).
Budget: hover precedent peek and Formula Explorer sub-expression click ≤32 ms.
Budget: view switch (Ctrl+1..5) ≤100 ms warm (≤200 ms initial synthesis).

Unbreakable invariants under any load: never freeze UI thread or ignore Esc; never silently truncate rows/sheets without an explicit count badge; never collapse a block in a way that conceals an interior #Error, broken external link, or hardcoded override.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Skins customise how DNA Calc looks, arranges and operates—never what Excel calculates—stored as validated declarative JSON (.dnaskin.json) in workspaces or schema-validated XML inside xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Four declarative skin sections (zero code): (1) theme (base Strand theme + WCAG AA contrast-validated surface/accent overrides), (2) views (per-workbook/sheet preferred view, density, chrome toggles, frozen rails), (3) layout (Notebook prose/slices/flow, Model Map groups/positions/Directors, App controls/KPIs/baseline/print), and (4) ergonomics (keymaps, palette aliases, pinned panels).

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Custom coded UI widgets ship strictly as signed host-installed Web Components receiving read-only cell values and emitting standard cell-edit intents—never as raw code inside .xlsx files.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Skin edits apply live in a reversible Skin Preview Seam ([Previewing Skin · Esc to Revert · Save to Workbook | Save for Me]), rejecting WCAG AA or semantic-signal violations with line-numbered fix hints.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API

Optional view-aware host bridge via Application.Run('DnaCalc.View.Switch' | '.Select' | '.ShowPanel') degrades harmlessly under On Error Resume Next in Excel; macros can never suppress security banners, spoof error badges, or bypass App formula protection without dirtying audit trace.

Try typing `$2,400` onto Monthly Payment, then compare paying `$300/mo` extra against `$0` extra and prepare a 2-page PDF."* — Pass bar: `0` overwritten formulas; exact `$154,652` savings read aloud; 2-page PDF configured in `≤ 2 min`.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Push-back: never allow executable skin component code inside .xlsx files because corporate gateways trust macro-free .xlsx specifically for carrying no code; keep xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml 100% declarative and install coded components separately as signed workspace extensions with declarative fallback cards.

statement: Risk: heuristic mis-grouping merging adjacent tables on messy legacy sheets. Mitigation: strict R1C1 + header boundary checks, visible confidence pills, and 1-click [Split / Ignore] overrides persisted in customXml.

Risk: perceived sluggishness from volatile legacy models (OFFSET/INDIRECT dirtying 184k cells). Mitigation: off-thread async recalculation with non-blocking editing, Strip cost meter, and Inspector's 1-click [Suggest INDEX replacement for OFFSET] refactor preview.

Risk: Excel round-trip drift shifting rows/columns while dnaCalcViews.xml stays static. Mitigation: bind view targets to Defined Names + R1C1 structural fingerprints and reconcile moved blocks on open (or flag cards needing re-anchoring).
Open question 1 (Model Map backing storage): recommends cell-backed workbook-scoped dotted names (sheet-scoped only for template sheets) so workbooks look clean and non-blank in plain Excel.

Open question 2 (Excel round-trip view anchors): recommends dual anchors—defaulting to (SheetName, RangeAddress, HeaderLabelFingerprint, FormulaHash) in customXml to avoid littering Name Manager, with opt-in clean Defined Names (_dna.kpi_ebitda).
Open question 3 (Undo across VBA macros): recommends improving on Excel by snapshotting a copy-on-write workbook delta around pure workbook-mutating VBA runs so Ctrl+Z cleanly undoes macros.

Open question 4 (Standalone Formula Explorer persistence): recommends local auto-persistence of recent scratchpads, lightweight .dnafe.json test suites for add-in developers, plus [Export Test Bench as .xlsx].

Open question 5 (Agent autonomy): recommends always staging model edits [M] in interactive sessions while allowing live reversible [V] skin previews, and routing unattended CLI auto-commits to a branched copy (Budget.agent.xlsx).

statement: R-1 (One Shell Invariance): Switching between `Classic`, `Inspector`, `Notebook`, `Model map`, and `App` (`Ctrl+1`..`Ctrl+5`) shall keep the Mast, Bridge coordinates, Sheet Tabs, and Instrument Strip at fixed screen coordinates with zero layout jump.

R-2 (Contrast Gate): Every foreground-on-background text token across `cockpit-light`, `cockpit-dark`, and `high-contrast` shall pass WCAG 2.1 AA (`≥ 4.5:1` normal text, `≥ 3.0:1` borders, focus rings, and graphical badges), enforced by automated build assertions.

R-3 (Sacred Semantic Channels): `red` (`#D02A23`) shall appear *exclusively* on evaluation errors; `amber` (`#FFB301`) *exclusively* on active focus, selection, and live recalculation activity; `signal` (`#FF8001`) *exclusively* on external links, `RTD`, add-in UDFs, and volatile formulas; every color cue shall pair with a distinct geometric glyph (`[!]`, double-frame, `◈`, `[↻]`, `①②③④`).

R-4 (Motion Discipline): Only three transitions may animate (focus settle, topological recalc ripple, cross-view continuity halo), each `120–160 ms`, and all animations shall collapse to instant `0 ms` state changes when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active.

R-5 (Non-Blocking Quarantine): Opening a workbook containing VBA macros or missing external file links shall never present a blocking startup modal; macros shall default to blocked and missing links to cached values behind a keyboard-accessible Quarantine Bar (`Alt+Q`).

R-6 (Zero Microsoft Assets): No Microsoft icons, fonts (`Calibri`/`Aptos` bundling), or Ribbon chrome artwork shall be used; Struktur uses `Recursive`, `Recursive Mono`, and `Source Serif 4` with system fallbacks.

R-7 (Screen Reader & Full Keyboard Operability): `100%` of features across all five views, Quarantine Bar, Formula Explorer, and Agent Review Rail shall be operable via keyboard alone with ARIA grid/tree/region announcements for errors, view switches, and recalculation completion.

R-8 (Cross-View Selection Continuity): Switching views shall map the active `ModelTarget` (`Cell`, `Range`, `Block`, `Name`, `Table`) to its tightest visible projection in the destination view within `≤ 100 ms` and highlight it with the continuity halo.

R-9 (Modeless 1-Bit Editing & `Esc` Safety): Every editable target shall distinguish `SELECTED` from `EDITING`; pressing `Esc` during any edit, drag, wire gesture, `F9` sub-eval, or agent review shall restore exact prior workbook and view state.

R-10 (Formula Lens Losslessness): Toggling Formula Lens (`Alt+L`) shall present readable name/header substitutions and read-only `LET` structure without altering stored cell formulas unless the user explicitly invokes `[Refactor Cell to LET]`.

R-11 (Unified Cross-View Undo): One chronological Undo/Redo stack (`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`) shall record both `[M]` model mutations and `[V]` view/skin edits across all views without clearing on view switch; pure navigation and Explorer sandbox tests shall not add Undo entries.

R-12 (Excel Conformance): Classic view shall pass `100%` of the keyboard and mouse behaviours specified in **Appendix A**, including `F2` `Edit/Point` cycling, `F4` anchoring/repeat, `F9` sub-expression preview, `End` mode, `Ctrl+Enter`, fill-handle double-click, and notched `①②③④` range picking across sheets.

R-13 (Provenance Tints): Classic shall provide an instant toggle (`Provenance Tints`) visually distinguishing literal constants (`prov-const`), formulas, iterative cells (`[↻]`), and external/volatile/UDF cells (`◈` `prov-ext`), plus flagging hardcoded constants breaking an otherwise uniform R1C1 formula row/column.
R-14 (Off-Sheet Precedent Tab Badges): During `F2` edit/point mode, worksheet tabs containing referenced precedents shall display matching `①②③④` badges and scalar value previews when scalar.

R-15 (Root-Error Folding): Inspector shall group all workbook `#` errors topologically by upstream root origin cell, displaying exact downstream broken-cell counts per root and expanding trace paths on demand.

R-16 (Dual-Target Discrepancy Waterfall): Selecting two numeric cells (`Ctrl+Click`) that share upstream tables/sheets and opening Inspector shall compute and display structural coverage differences (such as truncated `SUMIFS` ranges vs full Excel Tables) and dirty criteria mismatches (such as trailing whitespace or text-formatted numbers).

R-17 (Hidden & Volatile Inventory): Inspector shall list all `xlSheetHidden` and `xlSheetVeryHidden` sheets, broken/active external links, VBA modules, and volatile (`OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`, `NOW`, `RAND`, `RTD`) fan-out counts alongside profiled stage recalculation durations.

R-18 (Pluto-Style Live Reactivity): Notebook prose `@chips`, inline controls, Data Frames, and charts shall recalculate automatically in topological dependency order upon any input change without manual "Run Cell" execution.

R-19 (Dual Flow Layouts): Notebook shall support both vertical document flow (`↓ Page`) and horizontal multi-stage flow (`→ Pipeline`), storing prose (`Source Serif 4`) and slice layout exclusively in `xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml`.

R-20 (Windowed Data Frames & Explicit Fold Counts): Tables or schedules exceeding `200` rows shall render as virtualised, scrollable Data Frames with sticky headers/totals; folded rows or assumptions shall always state exact hidden item counts (`[▸ +9 assumptions]`).

R-21 (Sheet-Truth Schematic): Model Map boxes and wires shall project directly from defined names, inferred R1C1 blocks, and host precedents/dependents; rewiring or editing a box formula shall rewrite the backing Excel formula via the AST Presenter/Interpreter (`LINKED_BOXES_SKIN.md`).

R-22 (Cell-Backed Authoring Default): Creating a new actor on Model Map shall allocate a structured cell row on the backing worksheet and bind a Defined Name to it so the saved `.xlsx` displays human-readable sheet content in desktop Excel.

R-23 (Cycle Gate & Explicit Directors): Closing a circular wire when Excel Iterative Calculation is `OFF` shall halt at a Preview Seam offering to enable `Ticks (Max=1)` or `Iteration (Max=100, Δ=0.001)` or cancel (`Esc`); active iterative self-loops shall display `[z⁻¹]` or `[↻ iter]` badges, and `IFS`/`SWITCH` mode cells shall offer state-diagram rendering.
R-24 (Formula Overwrite Refusal): In App View, calculated formula cells shall reject direct literal typing, preserving formulas intact and offering Goal Seek or switching to `Classic`.

R-25 (Baseline Pinning & Deltas): App View shall allow pinning a baseline state in memory (or `customXml`) and displaying live directional deltas (`▼`/`▲` + semantic text, never color alone) across KPI cards and chart overlays.

R-26 (In-Workbook Sandbox Isolation): Opening Formula Explorer from a cell (`Ctrl+Shift+E`) shall seed inputs from that cell's precedents and allow temporary "Sandbox Try" value overrides without mutating the workbook until `Ctrl+Enter` is pressed.

R-27 (Standalone Stripped Binary): `DNA Calc - Formula Explorer` (`dot-long` identity mark) shall launch in `≤ 50 ms` with zero workbook loaded, providing multi-line `LET`/`LAMBDA` editing, AST sub-expression values, Number Format & Conditional Formatting rule testers, automatic boundary probes (`0`, negative, array, `#N/A`), and shadow-copied `.xll` UDF hot-reloading (`Ctrl+Shift+R`).

R-28 (Open & Keystroke Latency Budgets): On a 40-sheet, 300,000-formula workbook (`Inherited.xlsm`), cached first paint shall complete in `≤ 250 ms`, background indexing in `≤ 1,500 ms` with zero UI hangs (`> 50 ms`), cell navigation/typing in `≤ 16 ms` p95, and hover peeks in `≤ 32 ms`.

R-29 (No Anomaly Concealment Under Simplification): Collapsed blocks, composite districts, and semantic zoom levels (`< 70%`) shall always bubble interior errors (`[! N err]`), broken links (`◈`), and formula overrides onto the parent summary badge.

R-30 (Honest Refusal With Way Forward): When Notebook, Model Map, or App declines automatic synthesis on an unstructured dense sheet (`> 25,000` ungrouped formulas or `> 500` ungrouped blocks), it shall state the exact reason and provide 1-click actions to scope a range or open Inspector.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: R-31 (Declarative Skin Safety): Skins travelling inside `.xlsx` `customXml` shall contain declarative data only (zero executable scripts), pass automated WCAG AA contrast checks, and never override error/focus/external signal tokens or security banners.

R-32 (Excel Round-Trip Anchor Resilience): `xl/customXml/dnaCalcViews.xml` shall preserve cleanly when opened and saved by Excel, and DNA Calc shall reconcile shifted rows/columns on re-open via Defined Name + header/formula fingerprints.

R-33 (Agent Staged Change-Sets): All interactive AI agent model mutations shall land in a copy-on-write Staged Change-Set grouped by R1C1 formula runs, display automated KPI impact diffs across scenarios before commit, support per-hunk `Accept`/`Reject`, and push hunk-atomic Undo entries upon commit.

R-34 (Daylight Vector Printing): All views shall print paginated vector layouts using `cockpit-light` tokens; Classic shall match Excel `PageSetup` (`PrintArea`, `PrintTitles`, breaks, fit-to-page) exactly.

R-35 (Reversible Macro Checkpoints): Running an enabled VBA macro shall batch UI repaints when `ScreenUpdating = False` and record a pre-run workbook snapshot so `Ctrl+Z` can revert pure workbook macro mutations.

C-1 (Immediate Cached Snapshot on Open): Open a workbook and immediately read sheet names, visibility states (`Visible`, `Hidden`, `VeryHidden`), grid dimensions, formatting, and last-saved cached cell values before full dependency indexing or recalculation completes.

C-2 (Security & External Inventory Up Front): Know on open whether the file contains VBA/macro modules, external workbook links (and whether their targets are reachable), `RTD` topics, or add-in UDF calls, and hold macros/broken links inactive until instructed.

C-3 (Cell, Name, and Block Precedents & Dependents): Query direct and transitive precedents and dependents for any cell, range, or defined name—including dynamic references (`INDEX`, `XLOOKUP`, `FILTER`, `OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`) resolved from the latest calculation—both at individual cell granularity and summarised by Defined Name, block, and sheet (preserving name-to-name edges rather than dropping names down to raw cells).

C-4 (Calculation Delta & Order Notification): Be told after every recalculation which cells and defined names changed value, what their previous and new values are, which external/`RTD` event or user edit triggered the pass, and a topological dependency ordering among changed items, plus elapsed time per sheet/stage.

C-5 (Root-Error Attribution): Given all cells currently holding `#` error values, know which cells are root origins (producing an error from non-error inputs) versus downstream propagations, along with the shortest error path from root to any dependent cell.

C-6 (R1C1 Formula Equivalence & Anomaly Detection): Group contiguous runs of cells that share an identical relative (R1C1) formula structure into single blocks, and be told of interior anomalies—such as a literal constant overriding one cell inside a formula run, or a range reference (`Orders!$I$2:$I$22000`) that covers most but not all rows of an Excel Table (`Orders`).

C-7 (Parsed Syntax Tree & Lossless Name Rewriting): Obtain the syntax tree of any formula (with character spans for every reference, literal, operator, and function call) and rewrite references bidirectionally between raw Excel syntax and scoped/shortened defined names without touching strings, comments, or function identifiers.

C-8 (Side-Effect-Free Sub-Expression & Sandbox Evaluation): Evaluate any selected sub-expression (`F9` in Formula Bar), complete scratchpad `LET`/`LAMBDA` expression, or temporary "what-if" input override (for Formula Explorer and Boundary Probes) and get back its exact value, data type, spill dimensions, number-formatted string, and conditional-formatting rule match—without mutating or dirtying the live workbook.

C-9 (Workbookless Standalone Engine Mode): Start the formula parser, 500+ built-in Excel functions, number formatter, conditional-format evaluator, and add-in UDF host with no workbook loaded at all (`DNA Calc - Formula Explorer`).

C-10 (Excel Calculation Mode & Iterative Parameters): Read and set workbook calculation mode (`Automatic`, `Automatic Except Data Tables`, `Manual`), `Iterative Calculation` enablement, `Maximum Iterations`, and `Maximum Change`, and trigger single recalculation steps (`F9` / `Shift+F9` / full rebuild) on demand.

C-11 (Dirty / Stale State Visibility): Know under `Manual` calculation mode (or mid-stream during large async recalculations) which cells and blocks are currently dirty/stale relative to upstream edits.
C-12 (Dynamic Spill Boundaries & Blockers): Know for every dynamic-array anchor cell its current spilled rectangle (`B14:E21`), or—if `#SPILL!` occurs—the exact cells blocking the spill.

C-13 (Native Table, Pivot, Data-Table & Control Metadata): Read and update Excel `ListObject` tables (headers, column names, total rows), `PivotTable` source ranges/axes/cached values, What-If `{=TABLE(row, col)}` definitions, charts, and Form Control bindings (`ScrollBar` min/max/step/linked cell).

C-14 (Custom XML View Part Round-Trip): Read and write arbitrary UTF-8 XML/JSON blobs in a dedicated custom part of `.xlsx` / `.xlsm` files that desktop Excel ignores and preserves intact across edits and saves.

C-15 (Structural Fingerprint Reconciliation): Compute lightweight label/formula fingerprints for ranges referenced by custom view settings so that if rows or columns were inserted in desktop Excel while DNA Calc was closed, moved blocks can be located on re-open.

C-16 (Copy-on-Write Staged Change-Sets): Apply a batch of proposed edits (from an AI agent or refactor preview) onto an isolated fork of the workbook, read the resulting diffs across all affected cells and summary KPIs, and selectively commit chosen subsets or discard with zero residual state.

C-17 (Atomic & Compound Undo/Redo Checkpoints): Group multi-cell fills, agent hunks, or VBA macro runs into named, reversible checkpoints that restore exact values, formulas, formatting, and calculation state in `O(changed cells)` time.

C-18 (Non-Locking Add-in UDF Host & Metadata): Load and unload `.xll` / add-in packages without locking their files on disk, enumerate exported function names, argument descriptions, return types, thread-safety, and volatility flags, and store portable `_xll.` prefixes + cached results in `.xlsx`.

C-19 (Non-Blocking Cancellation & Viewport Priority): Keep viewport reads, edits, and `Esc` cancellation responsive while indexing or recalculating 300,000+ formulas in the background, prioritizing cells visible on screen or displayed in the Strip.

C-20 (Fast Aggregate & Criteria Mismatch Queries): Compute Strip aggregates (`Sum`, `Avg`, `Count`, `Min`, `Max`) over multi-thousand-cell selections instantaneously, and identify near-miss rows in a table column (e.g., `"West "` with trailing whitespace or text-stored numbers `"37000"`) when auditing `SUMIFS`/`XLOOKUP` discrepancies.

C-21 (Excel PageSetup & Print Geometry): Read and write Excel `PageSetup` settings (`PrintArea`, `PrintTitles`, manual/automatic page breaks, orientation, scaling) and query exact row/column pagination boundaries for `Classic` print parity.
C-22 (Goal Seek Single-Input Solver): Solve for a single numeric input cell needed to make a formula cell hit a target number (powering App View's safe `[Solve Principal for $2,400/mo…]` action).

Program recognition: **100% (Deterministic):** Native OOXML `pivotTableDefinition` + `pivotCacheDefinition`. Confirm/correct: Trigger `[Refresh Pivot]`, inspect cache staleness, or compare against `SUMIFS` cells (`M-04`). Views: **Classic:** Clean tabular Pivot rendering with field filter pills & stale-cache badge. **Inspector:** Verifies cache freshness vs source `Orders` rows (`M-04`). **Notebook:** Live summary Data Frame with interactive slicer pills. **Map:** `[Pivot: Region × Quarter]` aggregation node fed from `Orders`. **App:** Interactive cross-tab card with region/period filters.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #12 (**Live data** — (`Watershed` `RTD` feeds; `Inherited` external `.xls` & `OFFSET`)): Human sees: Real-time streaming `=RTD(...)`, external workbook links, web queries, or clock-driven volatile functions (`NOW`) pushing asynchronous updates. Program recognition: **100% (Deterministic):** AST contains `RTD`, external `[Workbook.xls]` references, or volatile functions. Confirm/correct: Hold/resume feed, inspect cached timestamp (`M-01`), or adjust throttle rate. Views: **Classic:** `◈` `prov-ext` (`#A35400`) glyph + optional 140 ms `amber` update flash. **Inspector:** Live Event Queue strip & external-link health table (`M-13`). **Notebook:** Timestamped live `@chips` (`As of 16:09:47`). **Map:** `Events` Director + `◈` source actors lighting only dirty downstream paths. **App:** Live ticker badge + `[Pause Live Feed]` freeze toggle.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #13 (**Macro-driven models** — (`Inherited`: VBA `Module1` `Roll_Month_End`)): Human sees: `.xlsm`/`.xlsb` files with macro buttons or `Worksheet_Change` hooks that copy/paste values, roll periods, or run custom VBA UDFs. Program recognition: **100% (Deterministic):** Presence of `vbaProject.bin`, shape macro bindings (`onAction`), or VBA UDF calls in formulas. Confirm/correct: Enable/keep quarantined per file (`Alt+Q`); inspect macro procedure names & button bindings. Views: **Classic:** Quarantine Banner on open (`M-01`); reversible `[M] Macro` Undo checkpoint when run. **Inspector:** Lists all procedures, macro-bound shapes, and VBA UDF dependencies. **Notebook / Map / App:** Surfaces safe macro trigger buttons *only* after user trusts macros; blocks silent execution.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #14 (**Reports & dashboards** — (`Budget`: `Summary`; `Sales`: `Report`)): Human sees: Presentation-oriented sheet combining formatted KPI callouts, variance columns, charts, and zero raw data storage—purely downstream of model sheets. Program recognition: **≥88% (High):** Terminal sink sheet (`0` or minimal downstream dependents on other sheets) holding charts, summary `SUM`/`SUMIFS` cells, and rich number formatting. Confirm/correct: Mark as `preferredView: notebook` or `app`; select headline KPIs for Agent Impact Banner (`M-10`). Views: **Classic:** Print-ready grid layout with clean chart rendering. **Inspector:** Default starting anchor for backward root-cause traces (`M-02`, `M-04`). **Notebook:** Executive Headline KPI Strip + charts. **Map:** Rightmost sink district. **App:** Automatically populates Outcome Cards & charts (`M-16`).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #15 (**Stocks, flows, feedback & delays** — (`Stock`: `OnHand`, `Inflow`, `Outflow`, `DelayPipe`, `IFS` Mode)): Human sees: State accumulation (`Stock[t] = Stock[t-1] + Inflow - Outflow`), multi-step pipelines (`DelayPipe`), and threshold policies (`ReorderPoint`, `IFS` state guards) forming closed feedback loops. Program recognition: **≥85% (High):** Self-referencing additive state formulas (`X = X + A - B`), shift arrays (`HSTACK(DROP(...))`), and closed precedence cycles through `IF`/`IFS`/`MIN`/`MAX`. Confirm/correct: Confirm state variables (`[z⁻¹]`), pipeline length, and modal `IFS` state cells (`M-15`). Views: **Classic:** Clean backing table with `[↻]` iterative tags & spill borders (`M-06`). **Inspector:** Loop gain/stability & tick-order trace. **Notebook:** Systems write-up with equation Lens & live step chart. **Map:** Native home—`Ticks` Director, `[z⁻¹]` delay arcs, `IFS` state machine pills, History Plotter (`M-05`, `M-15`). **App:** Interactive policy simulator with slider + time-series plot.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #16 (**Reconciliation & check blocks** *(Added)* — (`Sales` / `Budget` tie-out rows: `=ABS(C9-N12)<0.01`)): Human sees: Dedicated `"Check"`, `"OK / ERROR"`, or `"Variance"` cells testing accounting identities (`Assets - Liab_Eq = 0`, `Sum of Regions = Total`) to catch silent drift. Program recognition: **≥90% (High):** Formulas comparing two aggregates via `ABS(A-B)<ε`, `ROUND(A-B,2)=0`, or `IF(A<>B, "ERR", "OK")`, or rows labelled `Check`/`Tie`/`Diff`. Confirm/correct: Pin check cells to the **Workbook Health Strip** so any edit anywhere that trips a check alerts immediately! Views: **Classic:** Highlighted check badge; trips show `[⚠ Check Failed]` in Strip even if no `#Error` exists. **Inspector:** Dedicated **Model Checks** probe auto-monitored on every recalc. **Notebook / App:** Quiet `[✓ All 4 Checks Balanced]` footer badge (turns `amber`/`red` if tripped). **Map:** Guard assertion node wired from compared blocks.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #17 (**Ragged hierarchies & rollups** *(Added)* — (Multi-level Chart of Accounts / `SUBTOTAL(9,...)` trees)): Human sees: Indented category trees where parent rows sum child blocks of varying depths—dangerous when someone writes `=SUM(C4:C40)` and accidentally double-counts subtotals! Program recognition: **≥88% (High):** Nested `SUM` ranges sitting inside outer `SUM`/`SUBTOTAL`/`AGGREGATE` spans, paired with leading-space or indent-level row labels. Confirm/correct: Confirm hierarchy levels or repair double-counted `SUM` -> `SUBTOTAL(9, ...)` via Preview Seam. Views: **Classic:** Collapsible outline gutter (`1 · 2 · 3` levels) + double-count audit warning. **Inspector:** Flags overlapping `SUM` double-count bugs immediately. **Notebook / App:** Expandable tree table (`▸ Operating Expenses`) with accurate rollups. **Map:** Nested tree rollup block.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #18 (**Dynamic array spill pipelines & `LAMBDA`s** *(Added)* — (`Sales` `SORT(FILTER(...))` `M-17`; named `LAMBDA`s)): Human sees: Single top-left formula cell (`B14`) dynamically spilling variable-sized 2D results (`B14#`), chained via `#` spill references, `LET`, `MAP`, `SCAN`, `REDUCE`, or custom `LAMBDA` names. Program recognition: **100% (Deterministic):** Dynamic array AST operators (`#` spill range, array-returning functions, workbook `LAMBDA` defined names). Confirm/correct: Inspect/debug in Formula Explorer (`Ctrl+Shift+E`); promote repeated `LAMBDA`s to named helpers. Views: **Classic:** `teal-600` spill frame; `#SPILL!` highlights exact blocking cell. **Inspector:** Tracks dynamic `#` resize cascades. **Notebook:** Auto-sizing live Data Frame expanding cleanly as `FILTER` row count changes. **Map:** Reusable `LAMBDA` shown as an `[Actor Class]` badge; spills show live `[R × C]` dimension pill. **App:** Self-sizing result table (zero blank padding rows!).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern #19 (**Override & manual-adjustment layers** *(Added)* — (`Inherited`: `47` hardcoded cells inside `Gas_Daily_2001` formula cols)): Human sees: A literal number (`$140,000`) or one-off `+ 5000` plug typed directly over one cell (`Monthly!I17`) in the middle of an otherwise uniform 12-column formula row! Program recognition: **≥94% (High):** Single cell (or small island) whose R1C1 signature (`Constant` or `Formula + Plug`) breaks the surrounding `≥5`-cell row/column equivalence class. Confirm/correct: Mark `[✓ Intentional Override (Documented)]` (adds clean note) or `[Restore Row Formula]` (`Ctrl+R` preview). Views: **Classic:** Unmistakable notched corner flag on `Provenance: ON` so overrides never hide. **Inspector:** Listed in Hygiene Radar (`47 hardcoded overrides` `M-13`, `Alt+R` jumps through them). **Notebook / Map:** Collapsed block header explicitly warns `[! 1 manual override at Jul-27]` (Principle 2: never summarize away an anomaly!). **App:** Protected from accidental creation by end-users.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Wireframe visual conventions double as the design's non-colour cues so every signal remains legible without colour.
why: Ensures no information relies on colour alone.

statement: Selection and 'now' are encoded as an amber outline (#FFB301), the sole saturated attention channel (wireframe cue: ▐ … ▌).
why: Reserves saturated amber strictly for current focus and selection.

statement: Facts stated in the workbook file use solid lines and plain names in ink (#353938) and teal (#318995) for structure.
why: Distinguishes workbook truth from program inference.

statement: Items inferred by the program rather than stated in the file use dashed teal lines and guillemet labels ‹label›.
why: Makes inference visibly distinct from file-stored facts.

statement: Proposed or previewed items not yet in the file appear as ghosts using dotted teal lines and slanted/casual type.
why: Separates uncommitted previews and proposals from committed workbook state.

statement: Errors are marked by a red tick (#D02A23) on the cell's left edge alongside Excel's error text; red means nothing else.
why: Keeps red unambiguous and leaves the cell's own formatting untouched.

statement: Cells fed from outside data or volatile functions carry the ◊ glyph in signal orange (#FF8001, text #A35400).
why: Makes external links, RTD, add-ins and volatility immediately visible.

statement: Values changed in the most recent recalculation show a fading green underline (#3F8B76) (wireframe cue: •).
why: Gives transient feedback on what moved after recalculation.

statement: Warnings have no colour hue of their own and use bold ink with a hollow triangle ([!]).
why: Avoids adding another hue to the signal palette.

statement: Cast workbook reference figures are pinned across mockups: Budget 2027 (Base rev 3,940,602 / costs 3,017,387 / op profit 923,215; Downside 3,255,671 / 2,689,858 / 565,813), Sales (Report!D9 1,204,318.50 vs Pivot 1,251,907.25), Loan (250,000 at 6.50% / 30y, payment 1,580.17), Stock (Store.Stock, Supply.ReorderPoint, 1 pass/recalc), Inherited.xls (40 sheets, 301,482 formulas, Curves A1:IV900, 2/5 links missing, Module1, 4,226 errors from 3 roots, manual calc).
why: Ensures consistent, verifiable numbers across every mockup and test script.
evidence: Cast workbooks: Budget, Sales, Loan, Stock, Inherited

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Fable adds petrol-800-scoped chrome ink tokens (--c-ink #EDF1F2, --c-meta #A9C0C7, --c-teal #4FC0D8, --c-green #74C7AB, --c-ext #F0A35C, --c-red #FF9C96, --c-const #7DB8D8) on top of Strand's cockpit-light tokens because Strand specifies ink variants for dark paper but not for petrol-800 chrome.
why: Maintains contrast for signal inks rendered on dark petrol chrome bands.

statement: Three dressed component renders illustrate the live visual grammar: cell states on paper (typed constants in constant ink, amber selection with fill handle, green underline for fresh, red left tick for errors, signal orange ◊ for external, diagonal hatch for as-saved, dotted teal italic for ghost), line-style truth chips (solid name, dashed inferred label, dotted ghost, amber active caret), and the always-present petrol Strip.
why: Shows how the wireframe symbols translate to styled surfaces and contrast-checked tokens.

statement: 'Modern on the surface' does not mean new paint on a grid, fewer features, or decorative animation; it means four concrete capabilities Excel's surface omits.
why: Anchors modernisation in user-visible clarity and honesty rather than cosmetic styling.

statement: Structure is visible: blocks, runs of like formulas, names, tables and flows are read from the file and shown as selectable objects to point at.
why: Makes hidden spreadsheet architecture legible without manual annotation.

statement: State is visible: calculation status, errors and their roots, uncalculated values, outside data and change provenance are standing instruments rather than modal dialogs.
why: Keeps truth about the workbook continuously visible instead of buried in pop-ups.

statement: Consequences come before commitment: every edit previews what it will write to the file before Enter (the preview seam), and Esc is an exact revert.
why: Prevents silent model damage from edits made in higher-level views or Classic.

statement: The reader picks the surface: five views show one workbook to five kinds of reader while the file stays plain Excel and the grid remains one key away.
why: Matches presentation to task without splitting the underlying workbook or locking out Classic.

statement: Honesty is a hard constraint rather than a weighted quality: no view may show a value, formula, dependency or state unsupported by Excel-faithful calculation; views that simplify must say so in place with counts, and views that cannot be truthful must decline with a way forward.
why: Prevents misleading simplifications across all views.

statement: Quality priorities differ by view under the honesty constraint: Classic ranks familiarity > density > clarity; Inspector and Model map rank clarity > density > familiarity; Notebook ranks clarity > familiarity > density; App ranks clarity > familiarity with the task > density.
why: Resolves trade-offs cleanly for each persona and view.

statement: Outside Classic, familiarity means preserving Excel's formula language, editing keys and terminology rather than copying the grid layout.
why: Lets non-grid views stay intuitive to Excel users without imitating spreadsheet chrome.

statement: Every view shares one shell built from Strand's Mast, Bridge and Strip plus a single-row command Deck.
why: Prevents the five views from feeling like five separate applications.

statement: Every view shares one selection, one address field in Excel terms, and one formula bar where F2 edits the selected item's formula with all Classic formula keys.
why: Guarantees continuity of place and editing skill across views.

statement: Every view shares one edit grammar (type to replace, F2 to edit, Enter to commit, Esc to revert, Tab to commit and move), and SELECTED vs EDITING states show simultaneously in three places: the item, the formula bar, and the Strip.
why: Eliminates mode confusion across views.

statement: Every view uses one unified signal vocabulary: amber for now, red for error, signal orange for outside/volatile data, green for fresh, teal for structure, each paired with a shape, plus line style (solid stated, dashed inferred, dotted ghost) as a second channel.
why: Ensures consistent interpretation and accessibility without relying on colour alone.

statement: Every view shares one peek card, one set of docked panels (Details, Trace, Changes, Issues, Outline, Watch), one workbook undo history, one command palette (Alt+Q), and one Esc ladder that steps back exactly one level.
why: Keeps auxiliary tools and escape behaviour predictable everywhere.

statement: Excel's shortcuts remain untouched; all ten DNA Calc-specific shortcuts live on the Alt+Shift layer: 1-5 for views, 0 for grid alongside, L for lens, E for Formula Explorer, T for Trace, and D for Details.
why: Avoids colliding with Excel muscle memory while keeping new capabilities easy to remember.

statement: The shared shell (M0.1) comprises seven regions: (1) Mast with file/state, five view tabs, and unified 'Ask or run… (Alt+Q)' field; (2) one-row Deck using Excel tab names and key-tip letters in DNA Calc styling; (3) Bridge with address field and formula bar (folded by default only in App); (4) paper Stage with the shared selection; (5) right/bottom docked Panel (Details = pinned peek card); (6) Sheet tabs in Classic (sections/pages/levels elsewhere); (7) never-hidden Strip showing mode, calc, errors, outside data, macros, agent, and statistics.
why: Provides a single, stable spatial frame across all five views.

statement: P1 (Truth before polish, highest precedence): simplify only visibly and decline rather than fake — e.g., draw a delay only where the system reports a last-pass read, show errors and causes on App tiles rather than blanks, report run exceptions as '11 alike, 1 differs', and label saved values 'as saved'.
why: Gives a deterministic tie-breaker when clarity or polish conflicts with honesty.

statement: P2 (One workbook, one pointer): selection, address, clipboard and undo belong to the workbook rather than to any view, so switching views never loses place and Ctrl+[/Ctrl+] mean upstream/downstream everywhere.
why: Keeps all views synchronized views of one underlying model.

statement: P3 (Every edit is an Excel edit, previewed): any model-changing gesture previews the exact cells, names or settings it will write, must be reproducible in Excel, and undoes as one step; non-model gestures are free presentation or refused (e.g., notebook sort is a view sort, prose quotes values without computing, sliders commit on release so iteration ticks once, App scenarios are Excel scenarios).
why: Protects round-trip compatibility with Excel and makes side effects explicit.

statement: P4 (Read the file first, ask second, always allow correction): the program infers blocks, labels, inputs and patterns automatically with visible evidence and confidence, stores corrections with the file, and never requires upfront declarations before a view works.
why: Makes views immediately useful on existing ordinary Excel files.

statement: P5 (Old hands lose nothing): Classic honours every Appendix A Excel gesture unchanged (e.g., Ctrl+` stays Show Formulas while lens takes Alt+Shift+L, Alt+Q opens the palette, key-tip paths preserve Excel letters), and no skin may lock the grid away.
why: Protects decades of Excel muscle memory.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: rename Strand's 'Inspector' panel to 'Details' because Inspector is now a full view.
why: Avoids naming collision between a docked panel and a top-level view.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: the paper belongs to the workbook author — Classic draws a cell's own formats (including author red) as Excel draws them, keeping Strand signals in gutters, edges, overlays and chrome; provenance tints are an optional overlay in Classic and default dress in other views.
why: Prevents DNA Calc styling from corrupting author-formatted spreadsheets in Classic.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: add line style (solid, dashed, dotted) as a truth channel alongside Strand tenet 2's single border treatment.
why: Encodes stated vs inferred vs ghost status structurally without adding colours.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: warnings have no hue (bold ink plus hollow triangle) and saved or stale values use a diagonal hatch rather than a colour tint.
why: Preserves colour-channel discipline and legibility without colour vision.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: a skin may carry a theme, but a theme consists strictly of token values, must pass contrast checks, and cannot re-bind any semantic signal.
why: Allows visual customisation without weakening accessibility or signal honesty.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: cap the recalculation ripple at 400 ms total, stepping by block beyond 200 items, and do not animate a marching-ants copy outline.
why: Respects Strand's strict animation budget and prevents sluggishness on large sheets.

statement: Refinement to Strand v0.1: the agent has no dedicated hue of its own; its marks are teal, dotted and badged, never amber.
why: Keeps amber exclusively for the user's current selection and focus.

statement: Storyboard steps are numbered with exact keys and time budgets so they double as executable usability test scripts and requirement citations.
why: Ties narrative design directly to verifiable acceptance tests.

statement: First-run start page (M1.1) presents three verbs with keys (Open workbook Ctrl+O or drag-and-drop anywhere on the window, New workbook Ctrl+N, Formula Explorer Alt+Shift+E), a Recent list, a one-line compatibility promise ('Your file stays an Excel file. Nothing is added that Excel cannot open'), and the discovery rule ('Everything you know from Excel works in Classic. What is new is on Alt+Shift and Alt+Q').
why: Reassures cautious Excel users immediately and establishes the two-layer keyboard model on day one.

statement: Staged non-blocking open (M1.2): file name and sheet count appear in the Strip within 100 ms; the previously active sheet paints from saved values within 2 s for Inherited-scale files and is immediately scrollable/selectable while remaining sheets stream in; no modal dialogs interrupt for links, macros, or manual calculation—instead one non-blocking notice line summarises all notices and auto-opens the Overview panel with live 'so far' counts.
why: Eliminates Excel's startup dialog wall while keeping large files immediately responsive.

statement: When a workbook opens in manual calculation, nothing recalculates automatically; a hatched band marks values 'as saved <date> · not recalculated here · F9', error cells keep Excel's text with a red left tick, file macro buttons render and explain themselves when macros are off, and screen readers announce file name, sheet count, calculation mode, notice count, and F6 for Overview.
why: Prevents users from mistaking stale cached values for freshly calculated numbers.

statement: Pressing Alt displays Excel's exact key-tip letters on the Deck (and Q on the palette), honours paths typed from memory without waiting for tips to draw, shows digits 1-5 on the view tabs for Alt+Shift, and displays a one-line summary of the Alt+Shift layer on the first five uses of Alt.
why: Teaches DNA Calc's new shortcut layer in place through an existing Excel habit.

statement: From Overview › Errors, errors are grouped by root cause (e.g., 3 roots explaining 4,226 errors) with impacted cell counts; Enter jumps directly to the root cell, Alt+← (and browser Back) navigates back to the prior place, and Ctrl+C copies the root list as plain lines with addresses for email.
why: Turns thousands of cascading formula errors into a small actionable list.

statement: Model map at sheet zoom (Alt+Shift+4, within 150 ms) shows all sheets with the active sheet outlined in amber, missing external links in signal orange with dashed wires noting 'values as saved', standing counts per box (formula count, packed, errors), identical-formula sheets collapsed into a stack (e.g., Jan…Dec 12 alike), hidden/very-hidden/unread sheets explicitly counted in side buckets, and an accounting footer ('40 of 40 sheets accounted for · 62 links in 9 bundles · cells are not drawn at this zoom').
why: Gives an honest architectural overview of large workbooks without dropping sheets or shrinking text.

statement: On the Model map, semantic zoom (sheets · blocks · cells) keeps text at constant size; Ctrl+[ lights upstream wires one hop per press, hovering a wire bundle shows a peek card with reference count and example formula, Enter drills into a box (e.g., Curves as 6 blocks, never raw cells), Esc steps back out, and Space peeks at a hidden sheet under a non-mutating band ('Hidden in the file. You are looking, not unhiding').
why: Lets auditors inspect structure and hidden sheets safely without modifying the file.

statement: Clicking a workbook button when macros are off runs nothing and opens an inline card at the button naming the procedure, line count, and static summary of actions (e.g., opens 2 workbooks, copies 6 ranges, saves), with 'Read the code' and 'Allow macros this session' actions.
why: Explains macro refusals transparently in context instead of silently failing or forcing a blind enable prompt.

statement: Editing a cell sets the Mast state to 'edited', and undoing back to the file's opening content restores the Mast state to 'unchanged'.
why: Reflects exact workbook identity rather than a latched dirty bit.

statement: During manual recalculation (F9), the Strip turns amber with progress and 'Esc stops', the grid stays interactive while waiting cells remain hatched, and completion reports duration, how many values differ from the saved cache (linking to the diff list), and how many external links used saved values.
why: Keeps long recalculations interruptible and exposes silent drift from cached file values.

statement: Ctrl+wheel zooms the stage; below 40% zoom on packed sheets like Curves, unreadable cell text gives way to legible block outlines with labels, and high-contrast themes preserve the error tick, ◊ glyph, and hatch because each is a shape.
why: Preserves semantic legibility at low zoom and accessibility in high contrast.

statement: First-open value proposition for Excel users: no startup dialogs, explicit 'as saved' labelling, error counts reduced to root causes, read-only peeking of hidden sheets, and true 'unchanged' state after undo.
why: Summarises the user-visible wins of Storyboard 1.

statement: On first visit to Notebook for a workbook without one (M2.1), the empty state offers a draft built from the program's reading ('By sheet, in order', 'Conclusions first', or 'Blank page'), lists what was read with a 'Why these?' link, confirms drafting changes nothing in the workbook, maps the active selection into the drafted outline within 400 ms, and states in the Strip where the selection landed while keeping Mast state 'saved'.
why: Avoids blank-page friction while proving that drafting is pure presentation (P4, P3).

statement: Reordering notebook sections via the Outline panel (F6, arrows, Alt+↑/Alt+↓, or drag handle) changes only presentation and updates the Mast state to 'saved, layout edited' to show the model is untouched.
why: Separates presentation edits visually from workbook model edits.

statement: Notebook text items (Alt, N, T) support inline live cell quotations (typing '=' and clicking a figure) that recalculate automatically, but refuse inline calculation expressions in prose with an inline offer to quote an existing cell or add the formula to the workbook.
why: Enforces P3 so no calculation ever hides outside the Excel model.

statement: Turning on the formula lens (Alt+Shift+L) renders defined names plainly and sheet-inferred labels inside guillemets (‹…›); right-clicking an inferred label offers 'Make it a name…' with a preview seam showing the Define Name and Apply Names scope; folded sections still surface run exceptions (e.g., 'People: 11 alike, 1 differs (Jun)').
why: Bridges readable labels and genuine Excel defined names while keeping exceptions visible.

statement: Editing a formula run item in Notebook (M2.2) edits all cells in the run (e.g., Monthly!C8:N8) as one formula with typo autocomplete suggestions, opens a dotted preview seam stating exact cell range, Excel formula text, result range, and whether values change, commits all cells as one undo step on Enter (exact revert on Esc), shows folded columns via a named control (◄ Mar–Nov ►), and propagates fresh marks through dependents and live prose quotations within 100 ms.
why: Prevents partial-row formula drift and makes multi-cell model edits safe from Notebook.

statement: Clicking a column header in a Notebook frame applies a labelled 'view sort ▲' that does not reorder the underlying sheet; copying a frame puts a formatted table for email and cells for Excel; pasting prose creates text items, while pasting an external table asks 'As text' (Enter) or 'As cells' with the exact target sheet range previewed.
why: Protects sheet data from accidental presentation sorts or unpreviewed pastes.

statement: Notebook 'Reading' density folds formulas to their names and sets prose in a serif reading face; Ctrl+P previews the write-up as a paginated document where each page footer carries the file name, active scenario, and value timestamp, and folded sections print as one-line summaries.
why: Produces director-ready narrative output tied verifiably to workbook state.

statement: Saving a workbook with a Notebook notifies once that it saved as an ordinary Excel workbook carrying the notebook inside (preserved and hidden by Excel) and sets Notebook (Reading density) as the workbook's preferred view.
why: Clarifies round-trip persistence for both DNA Calc and Excel recipients.

statement: Notebook accessibility: semantic headings map to real headings, formula items announce name, spoken formula, count and value range to screen readers, and at 200% zoom prose reflows while data frames scroll internally.
why: Meets screen-reader and low-vision zoom requirements without losing content.

statement: Notebook value proposition for Excel users: a row of twelve formulas behaves as one formula (preventing stragglers and surfacing existing ones), and prose figures stay live cell quotes that cannot drift from the model.
why: Summarises the user-visible wins of Storyboard 2.

statement: When exactly two numeric cells are selected (e.g., clicking Report!D17 and Ctrl+clicking Report!D9), the Strip automatically adds their Difference alongside Sum and Count.
why: Eliminates scratch-cell subtraction during quick reconciliation.

statement: Ctrl+[ keeps Excel's exact jump-to-precedents behaviour; returning via Alt+← restores the selection and, once per session, the Strip gently offers 'Alt+Shift+T traces without leaving the cell'.
why: Guides Excel power users from familiar shortcuts to DNA Calc's Trace instrument.

statement: Trace panel (Alt+Shift+T, docking under the grid within 200 ms, M3.1) explains conditional aggregation formulas (like SUMIFS) as a ladder of criteria tests showing rows remaining after each test and rows that 'fail only this' test, displays graded diagnostic hints (e.g., '[!] Hint, likely: 41 rows carry a time of day'), and aggregates the flaw across the entire matching formula run (16 cells, 412 rows, 478,930.15).
why: Surfaces the exact near-miss rows where spreadsheet reconciliation bugs hide.
evidence: S3.3, M3.1; Sales Report!D9 vs D17

statement: Pressing Enter on a Trace ladder row opens the source table under a labelled non-mutating 'View filter from Trace' (M3.2) that leaves Excel's AutoFilter and SUBTOTAL untouched, marks gapped row numbers in teal with an omitted-row count, shows both formatted display and raw stored serial value in Details/peek card (exposing hidden time-of-day decimals), and clears cleanly on Esc.
why: Lets auditors inspect filtered failure rows and hidden stored precision without altering workbook state.

statement: Opening Formula Explorer on a cell (Alt+Shift+E) pre-populates its precedents and lets the user edit a trial formula ('Trying. Workbook unchanged.') to confirm a fix (e.g., changing '<='&D$4 to '<'&E$3) without modifying the file; Esc discards the trial.
why: Allows auditors to test formula hypotheses safely on a reviewer's copy.

statement: Switching from a docked Trace panel in Classic to full-stage Inspector (Alt+Shift+2) preserves the open trace and selected ladder node; returning to Classic (Alt+Shift+1) restores the active cell and scroll position.
why: Connects docked panels and the full Inspector view seamlessly.

statement: When typing in Classic would overwrite a formula inside a uniform run, the preview seam warns before commit ('Replaces a formula with text. Breaks a run of 16 alike'), and Esc reverts cleanly.
why: Catches accidental formula overwrites before they corrupt a sheet.

statement: Ctrl+Shift+F2 records a finding as a standard Excel comment, and Ctrl+C inside the Trace panel copies an audit-ready outline plus the filtered rows table for pasting into Word.
why: Produces standard Excel annotations and external audit documentation.

statement: Selecting a PivotTable displays its last refresh timestamp and whether its source data has changed since refresh in Details.
why: Makes PivotTable cache staleness immediately verifiable.

statement: The Trace conditional ladder is exposed to screen readers as an accessible tree announcing test index, criterion, remaining row count, and fail-only-this count.
why: Ensures full audit workflows work without sight.

statement: Trace value proposition for Excel users: unlike Evaluate Formula (which collapses SUMIFS in one opaque step), Trace explains row-testing functions row by row, lifts number-format disguises, and tests fixes without touching the file.
why: Summarises the user-visible wins of Storyboard 3.

statement: Empty Model map (M4.1) teaches one grammar ('name = formula', e.g., Store.Initial = 400) and states that every box is a named cell on a visible sheet; typing on empty paper opens a preview seam showing the label cell, value cell, defined name, dotted-prefix inferred group frame (dashed because inferred), and a 'place it elsewhere…' option before commit.
why: Lets engineers sketch directly on the map while keeping every box standard Excel.

statement: Model map supports top-down sketching: within a prefix group (e.g., Store), short names resolve to that prefix (Stock -> Store.Stock); undefined names get dotted underlines and Enter offers 'Create empty boxes for both' or 'Commit as typed: Excel shows #NAME?'.
why: Supports whiteboard-style sketching without breaking Excel name semantics.

statement: While editing a box formula on the map (M4.2), clicking other boxes inserts their references and draws dotted ghost wires (whereas committed wires are solid and strictly derived from formulas); closing a circular loop while iteration is off presents an inline three-way choice at the box (turn on iteration with explicit Max 1 / 0.001 settings, keep without iteration as 0 with circular warning, or Esc back to editing) instead of Excel's modal dialog.
why: Turns circularity into an explicit, inspectable modelling decision.

statement: On a circular loop with iteration enabled, the frame displays an Excel-terms calculation chip ('iterates · 1 pass per recalculation'), a self-reference carries a certain delay mark [z-1], and a cross-box wire carries a delay mark only where the engine reports a last-pass read (C-21); if the engine cannot confirm, the loop is drawn with no delay claimed.
why: Enforces P1 honesty: never infer or fabricate a delay mark unsupported by evaluation order.

statement: Dragging the source end of an existing wire onto another box previews the exact formula reference rewrite ('In Store.Sales: Demand becomes Supply.Order', showing before and after formulas) and Esc cancels with zero change.
why: Makes visual rewiring map cleanly and safely to concrete Excel formula edits.

statement: Adding a Slider control on a map box (Alt, N, Control › Slider) previews adding a standard Excel scroll bar form control linked to the box's cell; dragging shows a ghost value and commits once on release so iterative models tick exactly once.
why: Prevents slider drags from triggering dozens of unintended iterative ticks while staying standard Excel.

statement: Pressing F9 steps an iterative model by one tick, animating amber through boxes in evaluation order before settling with fresh marks; the iteration chip offers 'Repeat F9, 4 per second', and any box can be pinned to Watch to plot its history.
why: Makes iterative dynamics observable in real time using Excel's native F9 calculation.

statement: Alt+Shift+0 opens Classic grid alongside the Model map (M4.3) with one shared selection and formula bar so edits in either pane update the other immediately, solid delay marks and calculation chips remain visible, the Strip continuously states calculation mode and tick count, and Alt+Shift+1 + Ctrl+` inspects every raw Excel formula full-screen.
why: Provides instant verification that the visual model is a plain Excel worksheet.

statement: Undo handles both model and per-view layout steps: Ctrl+Z in Map undoes a box drag as '(layout)', whereas Ctrl+Z in Classic skips Map layout steps because layout changes are invisible from the grid.
why: Prevents invisible undo actions in views that cannot see another view's layout.

statement: Saving a map-built workbook confirms that names, formulas, iteration settings and sliders are standard Excel while map layout travels in the file and is ignored by Excel, so F9 in Excel produces identical numbers.
why: Confirms full round-trip fidelity of map-authored models.

statement: Model map keyboard, screen-reader and clipboard rules: arrows move spatially, Ctrl+]/Ctrl+[ follow wires, Enter/Esc drill in and out, screen readers announce box name, role, value, inputs (including last-pass reads) and dependents, and Ctrl+C on a frame puts a picture for slides plus 'name = formula' text for editors.
why: Makes the graphical map fully operable without a mouse and interoperable with external tools.

statement: Model map value proposition for Excel users: circularity becomes a visible decision with settings on screen rather than a hidden dialog accident, and everything drawn is a readable standard Excel sheet.
why: Summarises the user-visible wins of Storyboard 4.

statement: A workbook preferring App opens directly in App from saved values within 1 s, shows 'Checking the numbers' then 'Up to date' in plain Strip wording, hides the grid and formula bar by default, displays a one-time orientation note, and derives its input fields and limits automatically from unlocked cells, labels, and validation rules.
why: Gives non-Excel consumers an approachable calculator surface grounded directly in Excel features.

statement: In App, Tab visits editable white input fields only; committing a new value updates outputs, charts, and schedules within 100 ms with fresh marks and a 'was <opening value>' comparison caption.
why: Makes sensitivity exploration crisp and keeps the baseline figure visible.

statement: App layout and validation refusal (M5.1): Mast retains file, 'View as ▼' to every view, Print, and Ask (F6/Alt reveals Deck and Bridge); invalid entries are refused inline at the field using the workbook's own validation rule and message, offering Tab for a likely fix (e.g., 6.5% for 65) and Esc for exact revert; long schedules show a windowed frame with explicit counts ('360 payments · showing 3 · all ►').
why: Replaces jarring modal error boxes with contextual recovery while keeping full workbook access one click away.

statement: App scenarios (M5.2) bind directly to Excel's Scenario Manager: scenario chips switch inputs (and mark 'edited' when modified), 'Compare with: Base' displays Base values and deltas inline on every output tile (in-place Scenario Summary), 'Save as scenario…' previews which changing cells will be saved to Excel's Scenario Manager, and 'Reset' restores all inputs as one undoable step.
why: Makes Excel's underused Scenario Manager intuitive without inventing a proprietary scenario store.

statement: When an input causes a calculation error in App (e.g., Term = 0 causing #NUM!), every affected output tile shows the error code, red tick, plain-language cause from the trace root, and an 'Undo my last change' action—never a blank or stale number.
why: Enforces P1 honesty even in simplified consumer-facing App views.

statement: Resting on an App output tile reveals its provenance summary, cell address (e.g., Loan!C9), and 'See the cells (Alt+Shift+0)' so the underlying grid is always one key away.
why: Preserves auditability and trust without cluttering the App surface.

statement: Printing from App (Ctrl+P, page 1 previewed within 300 ms, M5.3) formats a clean one-page answer with optional Compare column, lets the user include/limit long schedules while stating page cost (e.g., 'all 180 payments, 4 pp' vs 'first year' vs 'none'), and adds a footer tying paper output to file name, scenario, and value timestamp.
why: Avoids accidental 40-page spreadsheet printouts while preserving provenance on paper.
