statement: Classic keyboard/mouse acceptance uses a pinned Excel for Microsoft 365 Windows English/US build as oracle (locale-specific fixtures separately, never silently importing Mac/Web/2010/OS-reserved behavior, with no Microsoft icons/artwork); input routing strictly follows focused editor/menu/dialog → focused view → shell (disabled commands state why rather than acting differently), and Ctrl+F2 follows current Microsoft docs as formula-bar editing (not Print Preview; Ctrl+P always prints).
why: Eliminates ambiguous shortcut routing and outdated Excel profile collisions.

statement: A-01 [Alt or F10, no editor active]: Show key tips on the compact command strip; no model or selection change. Esc removes tips and restores prior focus.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-02 [Key-tip letters]: Follow the displayed path; show the remaining valid letters. Preserve familiar group initials F/File, H/Home, N/Insert, P/Page Layout, M/Formulas, A/Data, R/Review, W/View, L/Developer. Layout stays Strand.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-03 [Common key-tip sequences]: Support Alt,H,V,V (paste values), Alt,H,O,I (autofit columns), Alt,H,O,R (rename sheet), Alt,A,T (toggle filter), Alt,W,F,F (freeze panes); test each against the named baseline. Sequence is not a simultaneous chord.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-04 [Legacy Alt,E,S,V,Enter]: Paste values through Paste Special. Legacy paths are aliases, shown in command search; unknown paths do not guess a command.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-05 [F6 / Shift+F6]: Cycle view, command strip, open panels and status/zoom landmarks forward/backward; preserve the last focus inside each. Split panes are reachable.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-06 [Tab / Shift+Tab in controls]: Traverse controls in reading order; do not move the underlying active cell. In a composite list, arrow keys move its items.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-07 [Shift+F10 or Menu key]: Open the same contextual actions as right-click for the focused cell, block, object or sheet tab. Esc returns to that exact target.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-08 [F1; Ctrl+F1]: Open contextual help; show/hide the command strip, respectively. Neither obscures the current edit without retaining it.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-09 [Click a cell; Shift+click another]: Select one cell; extend a rectangle from the selection anchor. Expose address, dimensions, active cell and error state to assistive technology.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-10 [Drag through cells]: Grow a rectangular selection; scroll at viewport edges; show final dimensions before release. Dragging cell interior is distinct from dragging its border.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-11 [Ctrl+click/drag]: Add a noncontiguous area; an already-selected area can be removed. Do not collapse existing areas. Unrepresentable downstream operations explain their limitation. [KA2]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-12 [Arrow; Shift+Arrow]: Move active cell; extend from the fixed anchor. A selected table or spill is still navigable by real cell addresses.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-13 [Ctrl+Arrow; Ctrl+Shift+Arrow]: Move/select to Excel's next data boundary. Fixtures include blank islands, formulas returning empty text, hidden rows and the sheet edge. No semantic block detector may redefine this gesture.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-14 [Home; Ctrl+Home; Ctrl+End]: Row start; worksheet start; last used cell, respectively. Used-range formatting can put the last used cell beyond visible data; report that honestly.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-15 [End then Arrow]: Enter the visible End-navigation state and move to its next boundary; a completed movement clears that state.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-16 [Page Up/Down; Alt+Page Up/Down]: Move one viewport vertically/horizontally, preserving approximate relative position; frozen areas remain frozen.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-17 [Ctrl+Page Up/Down]: Previous/next worksheet in workbook order. Skip hidden sheets as Excel does; restore each sheet's own selection and scroll position.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-18 [Ctrl+Shift+Page Up/Down]: Extend grouped-sheet selection. Show a persistent Grouped sheets label and the affected sheet count before edits.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-19 [Ctrl+Space; Shift+Space]: Select column/row in the current context. In a table, the first Ctrl+Space selects column data; the second includes the column header. Test subsequent expansion and Shift+Space against the recorded baseline. [KA3]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-20 [Ctrl+A]: In a table: data, then the entire table including headers. Outside a table: current region, then its summary rows, then worksheet where applicable. In an editor select its text, not the worksheet. [KA3]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-21 [Ctrl+Shift+*]: Select the current region. Blanks determine its boundary; a guessed model block does not.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-22 [F8; Shift+F8]: Toggle Extend selection; enter Add to selection. State is explicitly named in the Strip, announced once, and canceled without mutation.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-23 [Enter/Shift+Enter; Tab/Shift+Tab inside a selection]: Move active position down/up or across/back within the selected area; retain the area. Single-cell Enter movement follows the user setting.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-24 [Ctrl+.; Ctrl+Backspace]: Cycle corners of a rectangular selection; reveal active cell without collapsing selection.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-25 [F5 / Ctrl+G / address field]: Go to `Monthly!B4`, a defined name, multi-area address or `Report!H4#`. Invalid, missing and protected targets get distinct explanations. [KA4]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-26 [Go To Special; Alt+;]: Select cells by a stated category; select visible cells only. Expose whether filtered/hidden cells are included. [KA4]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-27 [Mouse wheel; scrollbar; Scroll Lock]: Scroll without changing selection. Scroll Lock changes arrow behavior and has a visible/announced status, rather than looking like broken navigation. [KA5]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-28 [Ctrl+wheel; zoom field]: Zoom the worksheet about the focus while preserving the active cell; shell/text zoom stays separately available. At large zoom there is no lost command or trapped focus.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-29 [Printable text while a cell is selected]: Start replacement entry; old content remains recoverable with Esc until commit. Leading `=` starts a formula. Apostrophe permits explicit text.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-30 [F2 / double-click]: Edit the active cell with the caret at the end. If in-cell editing is disabled, focus its formula-bar editor. Selection outline and caret are visibly different.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-31 [F2 during formula editing]: Toggle Point versus Edit behavior: arrows select references in Point state and move the caret in Edit state. The Strip names the state. [KA1]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-32 [Ctrl+F2]: Focus/edit the formula bar; while editing, transfer the same draft between formula bar and in-cell editor. It must not print. [KA1]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-33 [Enter; Tab; Shift variants during entry]: Commit valid entry once, then navigate. A syntax error retains the draft and selection; no partial formula is silently saved.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-34 [Esc during entry]: Restore the exact pre-edit formula/value, selection and cell formatting. Once an entry has committed, use Undo; Esc is not historical Undo.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-35 [Ctrl+Enter with a selected range]: Apply the entry to the whole selection as one edit, with relative references adjusted from the active-cell origin. Example: entering `=A1*2` into C1:C3 with C1 active produces references A1, A2, A3. [KA6]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-36 [Alt+Enter]: Insert an in-cell line break; do not commit or create another worksheet cell.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-37 [Backspace / Delete in an editor]: Remove text around the caret. Delete in Select state clears contents, preserving formatting; Backspace starts replacement of the active cell.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-38 [Ctrl+Arrow; Home/End with an editor focused]: Move within text. Shift extends text selection; Ctrl+A selects editor text. Grid navigation must not leak through.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-39 [Formula autocomplete]: Offer Excel functions, names, table references and loaded add-in functions; arrows choose, Tab inserts, Esc dismisses. Completion is distinct from committing the cell. [KA7]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-40 [Shift+F3; F3]: Open function argument help; insert a defined name. Empty names list explains that no names exist and offers Define name.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-41 [Type `=SUM(`, then mouse-select B4:M4]: Insert `B4:M4` at the reference insertion point; numbered outlines link text to ranges without relying on rainbow colors. Type `)` and Enter to commit. [KA8]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-42 [Pick a reference on another sheet or open workbook]: Preserve the unfinished formula and its origin; generate the correct quoted qualifier. Returning focus does not commit accidentally. External links are marked. [KA8]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-43 [Drag reference outline/corner during editing]: Change the selected reference range in the draft; preserve its absolute/relative flags; update formula text and preview together. Esc cancels the entire draft. [KA8]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-44 [F4 with a reference active]: Cycle `A1` -> `$A$1` -> `A$1` -> `$A1` -> `A1`; selected ranges retain corresponding endpoint behavior. Structured-reference details follow observed fixtures, never a blind string rewrite. [KA6]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-45 [F4 outside editing]: Repeat the last repeatable command; if it cannot be repeated, label that state. Never enter formula edit merely because a formula cell is selected. [KA9]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-46 [F9 in a formula editor]: Replace the selected complete expression, or whole formula when appropriate, with its evaluated result in the draft. A visible `Draft contains evaluated values` notice offers Esc; Enter commits that replacement. [KA10]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-47 [F9 outside editing]: Recalculate dirty formulas across open workbooks in the current session; keep last completed results explicitly stale while working. Do not refresh external sources merely because F9 was pressed.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-48 [Shift+F9; Ctrl+Alt+F9; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F9]: Calculate active sheet; full calculation; dependency recheck plus full calculation. Show which scope was requested and cancellation state. [KA11]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-49 [Ctrl+`; Alt+=]: Toggle formulas/values display; propose AutoSum's range before commit. Neither is the richer Formula lens, and their labels must not imply that it is.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-50 [Ctrl+Shift+Enter]: Commit a legacy array formula over the chosen range; ordinary Enter uses dynamic-array semantics where applicable. Never auto-convert one kind into the other. [KA12]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-51 [Edit/delete an interior legacy-array cell]: Refuse partial mutation with the whole array address and `Select array` action. One undo reverses an allowed full-array edit. [KA12]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-52 [Select/edit a spill child]: Show anchor, spill extent and read-only formula projection. `Edit source` selects the anchor; do not silently redirect a Delete or paste to the entire array. [KA13]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-53 [Spill is obstructed]: Keep `#SPILL!` at the anchor; reveal the obstruction cells. Clearing blockers is an explicit worksheet edit with Undo, not automatic repair. [KA13]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-54 [Ctrl+Shift+"; Ctrl+'; Ctrl+; / Ctrl+Shift+;]: Insert the above cell's value; insert its formula text; enter current date/time. Values and formulas are distinguished before commit. Verify locale and reference behavior in the baseline.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-55 [Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X]: Copy/cut current cell selection with explicit extent. Keep the source marked until the operation ends. Copying editor text copies characters instead.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-56 [Ctrl+V; Enter with a copied range]: Paste at the active destination with Excel-compatible relative-reference adjustment for copies and identity-preserving move semantics for cuts; show a clipboard-format limitation before any lossy paste. [KA14]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-57 [Esc after copy/cut, before paste]: Cancel pending clipboard operation and source marching outline; do not erase source values. After paste use Undo.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-58 [Ctrl+Alt+V]: Open Paste Special. Support All, Formulas, Values, Formats, Comments/Notes, Validation, widths, number-format combinations, Transpose, Skip blanks and arithmetic operations with explicit choices. [KA15]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-59 [Ctrl+Shift+V under current profile]: Paste values; show exact destination and retained number-format behavior. Older-profile or host conflicts are disclosed in shortcut settings.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-60 [Paste from text/CSV/another program]: Expose delimiter, locale and type interpretation when ambiguous; retain leading-zero identifiers via Paste as text. An app's HTML table must not import executable content. [KA16]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-61 [Copy to another program]: Supply an ordinary readable table/text representation; Excel-compatible cell formats where the destination supports them. If formulas cannot travel, say that the exported representation contains values.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-62 [Copy between Classic and another DNA Calc view]: Source-cell selection copies cells; a view-item frame copies presentation inside this workbook. Notebook paste offers `Link existing cells` (default) or an explicit value snapshot. Grid paste writes cells. External clipboard text never promises an internal bound target.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-63 [Drag fill handle]: Preview destination and fill meaning: copy/series/date pattern. Release performs one edit; subsequent Fill Options can choose the other supported interpretation. Relative, absolute and mixed references behave correctly. [KA17]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-64 [Double-click fill handle]: Fill down to the reference application's inferred neighboring-data extent; show the affected range in the completed operation. Fixture: formula beside Loan's continuous periods 1-360 fills to period 360. Blank gaps, unequal neighbors, existing targets and filtered rows each require observed baseline fixtures. Do not invent a single universal stopping rule. [KA18]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-65 [Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R]: Fill down from the selection's top row / right from its leftmost column, including relative-reference adjustment and relevant formatting, as one operation. [KA17]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-66 [Drag a selected range's border]: Move cells, not a view item; a ghost shows target and overwrite consequences. Formula dependencies follow the same moved cells. [KA19]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-67 [Ctrl+border-drag]: Copy instead of move. A plus marker and `Copy cells` label track the modifier state through pointer release. [KA19]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-68 [Shift+drag; Ctrl+Shift+drag whole rows/columns]: Insert moved/copied rows or columns at the shown boundary. Modifier changes update the preview immediately. Noncontiguous row drag is refused rather than rearranged approximately. [KA20]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-69 [Border drag over occupied cells]: Follow the recorded overwrite-warning setting for conformance; never mislabel copy as move. The preview must reveal occupied destination cells even when no blocking confirmation is required. [KA21]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-70 [Ctrl++ / Ctrl+-]: Insert/delete selected whole rows/columns directly; for ordinary cells ask direction of shift. Multi-area, table, protected and array conflicts explain why they cannot commit.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-71 [Row/column boundary drag; double-click]: Set explicit size; AutoFit to contents. Different gestures cannot accidentally move worksheet data.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-72 [Ctrl+9 / Ctrl+0; corresponding Shift chords]: Hide/unhide rows/columns. Hidden indicators and count remain discoverable. If Windows reserves the unhide-columns chord, offer the displayed command instead of promising interception.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-73 [Right-click sheet tab; drag / Ctrl+drag tab]: Rename, move, copy, hide, unhide or delete using the shown action; Ctrl+drag creates a copy. Grouped-sheet state remains prominent.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-74 [Shift+F11]: Insert a worksheet at the baseline position and select it. Undo removes that insertion without affecting its prior neighbor.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-75 [Sheet protection or locked target]: Preserve the selection and explain which target prevents the edit. Do not partially paste a rectangle around protected cells without a separate explicit operation.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-76 [Ctrl+T / Ctrl+L in grid]: Create an Excel table from a confirmed extent and header choice. Existing table selection opens relevant table actions, not a nested table.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-77 [Tab from table's last data cell]: Follow Excel's table extension behavior and inherited calculated-column rules; one Undo restores the prior table extent.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-78 [Edit a calculated table column]: Show whether the formula will fill the column; preserve structured references and reveal any exception rows. Never treat it as a display-only map change. [KA22]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-79 [Ctrl+Shift+L; Alt+Down on filter header]: Toggle AutoFilter; open that column's filter menu. Filtering changes visibility, not data order. Visible row count is exact. [KA23]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-80 [Filter menu keyboard / sort command]: Search and toggle items by keyboard, preserve focus on return, and identify active filter conditions. A sort moves the full record, or requires an explicit partial-range choice. [KA23]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-81 [Ctrl+Alt+L]: Reapply applicable sort/filter after data changes. Keep the current row identifiable by its source address and report if it is now hidden. [KA23]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-82 [Ctrl+F3; Ctrl+Shift+F3]: Manage names; create names from selected labels. Show scope, exact definition, value/error and duplicate/invalid-name refusal. No hidden change of scope to resolve a collision. [KA24]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-83 [Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H]: Find/Replace with explicit Selection/Sheet/Workbook scope, formulas/values, case, whole-cell and wildcard choices. Replace All gives a count and one Undo group. [KA25]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-84 [Shift+F4 / Ctrl+Shift+F4]: Next/previous result using the retained search options; an unavailable result says so. Returning to results does not clear selection context.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-85 [Ctrl+1]: Format Cells for the current model selection; show number-format preview using actual selected data. Layout-only appearance settings use a different labeled command. [KA26]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-86 [Ctrl+B/I/U/5]: Toggle bold, italic, underline or strikethrough on cells, or selected text when editing. Red remains reserved for error chrome; imported cell formatting is preserved as workbook data.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-87 [Ctrl+Shift+~, !, $, %, ^, #, @]: Apply General, Number, Currency, Percentage, Scientific, Date, Time formats using the active locale and reference-profile precision. The value stays unchanged. [KA26]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-88 [Ctrl+Shift+& / Ctrl+Shift+_]: Apply outline border / remove outline border as defined by the reference profile. Distinguish workbook borders from temporary selection and dependency outlines.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-89 [Freeze Panes command]: Freeze rows above and columns left of the active cell; keep selection/navigation meaningful across frozen and scrolled areas. Split creates independent scroll panes. [KA27]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-90 [Insert PivotTable]: Confirm source, destination and aggregation. Existing PivotTable layout uses field controls; it is not presented as an ordinary editable result range. [KA28]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-91 [Alt+F5; Ctrl+Alt+F5]: Refresh selected PivotTable/connection; refresh all. Show which source is requested and last refresh time; missing credentials or files produce explicit retained-cache state. F9 remains calculation, not refresh. [KA29]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-92 [Pivot drill-through / expand-collapse]: Match supported Excel pivot actions, with the created detail sheet treated as a model change. Warn/refuse unavailable external details without inventing rows.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-93 [Alt+F1 / F11]: Create an embedded chart / chart sheet from selected data. Empty selection and unsuitable source produce a concrete range-picking state.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-94 [Select shape/chart; Tab; arrows; Ctrl+drag]: Select the object separately from cells; cycle objects, nudge, or copy it. Shape text editing captures text keys; Esc returns to object selection. [KA30]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-95 [Form-control slider by keyboard]: Change the linked cell using the control's min, max, increment and page increment; show the new linked value and recalc state. A macro-enabled control discloses its executable action.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-96 [Shift+F2 / Ctrl+Shift+F2]: Edit a note / threaded comment, respectively, where supported. Plain notes are not automatically converted into conversations.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-97 [Ctrl+K]: Insert/edit a hyperlink, preserving cell content; external navigation does not run a workbook macro.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-98 [Ctrl+Z]: Undo the last committed model or presentation transaction across all views. Uncommitted text uses editor undo first; navigation and recalc notifications are not edit-history entries.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-99 [Ctrl+Y / F4]: Ctrl+Y redoes when a redo branch exists, otherwise repeats a repeatable action according to context. F4 outside editing is Repeat, not Redo; in formula editing it anchors references. Toolbar labels name the action. [KA9]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-100 [Save after Undo; switch view]: Save does not clear DNA Calc history; switching view neither commits an invalid edit nor changes the undo target. This cross-view contract is deliberate.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-101 [Alt+F8 / Alt+F11]: Open macros / macro editor where available. Explain blocked execution and unavailable host capability; preserve the workbook module. No claim that arbitrary external side effects are undoable. [KA31]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-102 [Ctrl+N/O/S; F12]: New/Open/Save/Save As with standard dirty-document recovery. Recovered and read-only copies are explicitly named; unavailable add-ins do not disappear on save.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-103 [Ctrl+P]: Open print preview for the current view; `Worksheet print` remains a direct choice. Include calculation freshness, scenario and scope where material.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-104 [Ctrl+W / Ctrl+F4; Alt+F4]: Close workbook; close application. Offer save/recovery for dirty content; never treat a browser-tab close as a guaranteed cancelable app action.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-105 [Ctrl+F6 / Ctrl+Tab, desktop]: Switch open workbook windows/documents in the chosen desktop convention. Browser tab-switching remains browser-owned unless a tested profile explicitly supports otherwise.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-106 [Shortcut customization]: Show conflicts, affected contexts, baseline command and reset. Imported skins cannot override core recovery/escape or reserve a hidden action behind a familiar command.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-107 [Alt+Down on a validation cell]: Open its permitted-choice list; arrows navigate, Enter chooses, Esc keeps the old value. The same chord in the formula editor toggles completion, never a cell-validation menu.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-108 [Ctrl+E]: Run Flash Fill from the supplied examples when supported; disclose that outputs are literal values, not a new formula. If unavailable, state that directly. One Undo restores every affected cell. [KA32]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-109 [Trace Precedents / Dependents; double-click a trace]: Add one real dependency level; navigate the chosen dependency. Missing external workbooks and untraceable relationships have visible endpoints, not fabricated edges. [KA33]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-110 [Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+]; Shift variants]: Select direct precedents / dependents; extended variants select their transitive equivalents according to the reference profile. Cross-sheet and closed-file cases require explicit observed fixtures.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-111 [Ctrl+Alt+5, then Tab]: Enter floating-object navigation and cycle shapes; Esc returns to the grid selection. This supplements pointer selection rather than taking over ordinary Tab.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-112 [F7; formatting toolbar by keyboard]: Check spelling in the selection/sheet; traverse formatting commands without losing the cell target. All changes appear in the same workbook history.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-113 [Navigation through merged cells]: Treat the merged area as the visible selectable unit; expose its extent and top-left storage cell. Arrow, Tab, Shift selection, paste and unmerge match recorded fixtures. Never create independent hidden values in covered cells.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-114 [Edit while sheets are grouped]: Keep `Grouped sheets: Inputs, Monthly` prominent and show all affected source addresses in edit feedback. Ordinary entry retains its familiar commit; bulk preview states the cross-sheet consequence. Ungroup through a tab/context command; Undo restores the entire grouped edit.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-115 [Operate versus select a form control]: A normal click operates the control; right-click or the Selection panel selects it for editing without firing its action. Show control-selection handles distinct from a focused slider thumb. Move/resize and linked-value changes have separately named undo actions.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-116 [Status detail / date-system setting]: Expose selection aggregates, edit/calc state and the workbook's 1900/1904 date system in accessible status details. Changing date system is a previewed workbook setting edit, never an inference made by a skin or paste operation.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-117 [Conditional Formatting > Manage Rules]: Show current scope, rule order, formula anchor, Applies to range, format and Stop If True. Preview edits on real selected values; Apply commits one reversible rule change. Workbook rule colours survive theme changes.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-118 [Invalid direct entry under data validation]: Honor the saved alert style: Stop offers retry/cancel; Warning permits explicit acceptance, revision or cancel; Information permits acceptance or cancel. Retain the draft and message. Paste/fill cases follow recorded Excel validation behavior, not a newly invented universal rejection.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-119 [Worksheet zoom versus UI/page zoom]: Label worksheet zoom separately from shell/UI zoom. The former changes sheet geometry; the latter keeps text and commands accessible. The browser's page zoom remains usable. Test both together at 200% and 400%, with frozen panes, panels and active editing.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-120 [Alt+Q]: Focus command search; typing filters commands, arrows choose, Enter invokes, and Esc restores prior focus and selection. A browser-owned conflict has an explicit reachable alternative.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-121 [A1 / R1C1 reference style]: Change display/input style without changing selected source or formula meaning. Verify reference picking, F4, copy and fill in both styles; R1C1 text is not treated as A1 syntax.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: In browser hosts, publish a visible 'Browser shortcut differences' sheet classifying F1, F5, F6, F11, F12, Alt, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Page Up/Down, Ctrl+Shift+V, Ctrl+0, and Ctrl+wheel per browser/OS as same, explicit alternate, browser-owned, or unavailable capability; never promise universal OS/browser interception, keep Commands/Go to/Recalculate/Open/Save/Help keyboard-reachable, and preserve reliable browser tab/address/zoom routes.

statement: Keyboard/screen-reader conformance tests selected vs focused vs editing states, announces coordinates/headers/format/value/size/membership/protection/staleness and completion (not every recalculated cell), keeps full access at 200%/400% zoom, exposes hover help on focus, and preserves non-colour range/error/caret cues; verify across 19 required fixture families (data boundaries, blank islands, formatted empty ranges, merges, filters/hidden rows, noncontiguous selections, tables, spills, legacy arrays, protection, scoped names, cross-sheet picking, empty-text formulas, clipboard round-trips, drag/insert, interrupts, stale results, macros, unavailable add-ins) recording selection, values, formatting, structure, and Undo.

statement: C-1: Identify a workbook, sheet, cell/range, name, table and object, and tell whether a formerly identified source still exists after edits or reopen.
why: Preserve selection and bindings without guessing nearby replacements.

statement: C-2: Read exact formulas, stored values, formatted text, number formats, styles, errors, annotations and relevant workbook settings.
why: Show source truth and preserve imported presentation.

statement: C-3: Know whether a value is saved, current, dirty, calculating, cancelled or unavailable, and which completed document revision it belongs to.
why: Prevent stale or mixed-revision results from appearing current.

statement: C-4: Be told which cells/objects/settings changed after an edit or calculation, including formatting and changed spill shape.
why: Update all bound views without re-reading the entire workbook.

statement: C-5: Read available cells incrementally, with trustworthy progress and the distinction between empty, not yet loaded and failed to load.
why: Keep Inherited usable during opening.

statement: C-6: Read sheet/table/object inventories with hidden/protection state, used extents and complete-versus-partial counts.
why: Honest navigation and large-workbook overview.

statement: C-7: Know formula precedents/dependents, summarised by range/block, with unresolved, conditional and runtime-selected references distinguished.
why: Explain Sales and Stock without fabricating connections.

statement: C-8: Obtain exact dependency membership and exceptions behind a grouped formula run or edge.
why: Expand summaries and target a precise map edit.

statement: C-9: Inspect a formula's syntactic structure, reference identity, local bindings, evaluation location and exact source spelling.
why: Render a faithful lens and safely resolve a displayed alias.

statement: C-10: Distinguish cells, spill anchors/children, legacy array regions, tables, pivot outputs, protected cells and objects when deciding editability.
why: Make every view obey the same edit rules.

statement: C-11: Preview and apply normal Excel-compatible edits with exact old/new targets, reference adjustments, validation and affected scope.
why: Share one editing contract across grid, map, notebook and agent.

statement: C-12: Apply a related set of changes atomically, reject stale expectations, and report conflicts at their actual source.
why: Prevent partial agent acceptance and stale Explorer apply.

statement: C-13: Record reversible edits and meaningful undo units across both model and authored presentation, while identifying non-reversible effects.
why: Predictable global undo and honest macro history.

statement: C-14: Retain/recover committed work and unapplied drafts distinctly, with identities sufficient to avoid repeating accepted actions.
why: Safe restart without automatic re-execution.

statement: C-15: Evaluate a formula trial in an explicit caller/input context, and distinguish expression testing from replacing a formula in temporary workbook state.
why: Ade's UDF tests and Lee's genuine cycle preview.

statement: C-16: Say whether a provider can be safely previewed, requires explicit execution, needs workbook context, or has external side effects.
why: Avoid invisible execution while typing or reviewing.

statement: C-17: Enumerate add-in functions and their available metadata, provider/version, permission state and supported execution host.
why: Honest autocomplete, loading and missing-provider paths.

statement: C-18: Expose formula-result values separately from number-format and conditional-format evaluation, including reference anchors when needed.
why: Test formatting without confusing display with calculation.

statement: C-19: Expose actual calculation mode, effective scope, iterative settings, cycle members and any genuinely observed convergence/stop reason.
why: Distinguish Stock's circular reserve from its period lag.

statement: C-20: Supply observed calculation trace/order/concurrency only when available, separately from dependency relations and value differences.
why: Avoid a fictional recalc animation.

statement: C-21: Report external link/provider identity, source availability, last supplied value/time and refresh/connection state without silently refreshing.
why: Missing sources and live instruments remain honest.

statement: C-22: Report observed live updates and their timestamps/coverage, and tell whether intermediate events were coalesced or not observed.
why: Label retained histories and avoid false event causality.

statement: C-23: Perform exact filtering/contribution queries on the requested scope and disclose incomplete processing; retrieve bounded row windows with stable source targets.
why: Sales' exact audit and large table interaction.

statement: C-24: Read and operate actual PivotTables, chart objects, form controls, scenario records, validation rules and print settings.
why: Views reuse existing workbook mechanisms.

statement: C-25: Know macro/module presence, trust, execution availability, run boundaries and observed workbook effects; support optional presentation requests.
why: Keep macro-driven models usable and attributed.

statement: C-26: Save/load versioned optional view declarations and source bindings in supported files, preserving unrelated workbook parts.
why: Make preferred views travel without changing calculation content.

statement: C-27: Detect missing/unsupported presentation versions and provide preserved declarations for recovery rather than silently throwing them away.
why: Graceful fallback to Classic.

statement: C-28: Preserve/transfer ordinary clipboard content with source-origin, formula/value/text/format distinctions and declare loss at an unsupported destination.
why: Reliable cross-view and Excel/program copy-paste.

statement: C-29: Provide a consistent completed-result snapshot and all relevant filters/source statuses for printing or report export.
why: Avoid mixed calculation revisions on paper.

statement: C-30: Expose all commands, edit states, coordinates, labels, selections and statuses through accessible interaction surfaces.
why: Keyboard, screen reader and high-zoom parity.

statement: C-31: Cancel or bound long work, report uninterruptible operations honestly, and keep ordinary navigation/edit feedback responsive.
why: Meet §6 without inventing computation completion.

statement: C-32: Supply resource/coverage estimates and exact totals where available before expanding large graphs, tables or histories.
why: Useful simplification and plain refusal instead of hangs.

statement: C-33: Attribute proposed/accepted/manual/macro edits, compare revisions and compute a proposed reversal against current state.
why: Auditable agent collaboration and conflict-safe recovery.

statement: C-34: Distinguish unsupported capability from invalid workbook content, and preserve the original content even when this host cannot execute it.
why: Respect the brief's file compatibility and cross-host reality.

statement: Pattern inference uses three evidence levels — E (explicit workbook structure/observed formula fact, still not proof of business intent), S (structural suggestion), and W (weak semantic guess) — always paired with evidence disclosure and address; 'bound' means resolving to an existing cell/range/object, whereas any new formula, name, scenario, or chart is an explicit workbook edit.
why: Keeps pattern confidence transparent and distinguishes view bindings from model creation.

statement: P-01 Sheet as database (Sales: repeated order rows beneath one header; filtering, IDs, quantities, amounts). Evidence/limit: E for `Orders` Table and its declared range; S for rectangular ordinary ranges with consistent column types; neither proves key uniqueness or absence of subtotals. Confirm/correct: Accept row/header range; mark `Order ID` as a display key; show duplicate counts; exclude totals; do not convert to a Table without an explicit model edit. Views — Classic: Full Orders table; headers, filters, pinned columns; Inspector: Selected row/value provenance; type/duplicate/error summaries with exact scope; Notebook: Bound table with visible total/filtered count and row window; underlying data remains accessible; Model map: One Orders node with column/row-count ports; expand chosen fields; App: Approved search/filter/table panel; edit only allowed input columns.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-02 Inputs and assumptions (Budget: twelve labelled assumptions with Base/Stretch columns; Loan: principal, rate and term). Evidence/limit: E for validation and named ranges; S for constants feeding formulas; W from colour, border or words such as `Input`. Confirm/correct: Confirm editable cells, labels, units and scenario columns; exclude constants that are historical observations; show protection/validation independently. Views — Classic: Existing assumption cells and validation; Inspector: Input -> dependents; constants/protected state; Notebook: Labelled bound controls beside explanation; Model map: Input node or ports, exact cells on focus; App: Main input form with units, validation and source details.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-03 Calculation blocks (Monthly revenue and cost rows repeat across Jan-Dec). Evidence/limit: E for repeated relative formula structure; S for borders, labels and adjacency; a shared pattern is not proof of a shared business role. Confirm/correct: Show exact member ranges and exceptions; rename/split/merge visual grouping; retain hard-coded overrides as explicit exceptions. Views — Classic: Original rows/columns; exceptional formula visible; Inspector: One formula family plus exception list; Notebook: Formula block with result table and source range; Model map: Calculation block with grouped edges and member count; App: Selected outputs; advanced detail can reveal block.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-04 Time series across columns (Budget dates progress left to right; repeated monthly calculations). Evidence/limit: E for values and references; S for date cadence and repeated formulas; text `Jan` alone does not prove year, cadence or chronology. Confirm/correct: Confirm period row, order, date system context and units; distinguish actual dates from captions; reverse or skip periods only in presentation with a notice. Views — Classic: Original twelve columns, freeze labels; Inspector: Period-relative dependencies and exceptions; Notebook: Compact time table/chart, horizontal pipeline if chosen; Model map: Period-labelled block; expand a chosen period, do not duplicate an unbounded timeline; App: Bound chart and period selector, if selection already has a workbook meaning.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-05 Scenarios and sensitivity (Budget's Base/Stretch columns; Loan's alternative assumptions). Evidence/limit: E for existing What-If data tables or stored scenario structures; S for parallel columns; W that differing inputs mean scenarios. Confirm/correct: Name input/output sets; distinguish viewing an existing scenario from writing selected input cells; review new scenario tables as workbook edits. Views — Classic: Existing scenario cells/data table; Inspector: Compared inputs/results with calculation state; Notebook: Side-by-side bound scenario results; Model map: Parallel input sets feeding the same calculation block; App: Explicit `Try`/`Apply` behavior with baseline and changed-input list.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-06 Reference tables and lookups (Sales product/customer mappings, XLOOKUP keys and return columns). Evidence/limit: E for lookup arguments/table structure; S for key-like columns; duplicate keys and approximate matches may be intentional. Confirm/correct: Confirm key and descriptive fields; reveal duplicate/missing keys and actual match mode; never silently deduplicate or sort. Views — Classic: Lookup table/filter and source formulas; Inspector: Match mode, actual matched rows, duplicate/missing-key warnings; Notebook: Lookup explanation and bounded reference table; Model map: Reference-table node, actual lookup dependency; App: Validated chooser with key/label and missing-key errors.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-07 Pipelines across sheets (Inputs -> Monthly -> Summary; Orders -> Report). Evidence/limit: E for resolved dependencies; S for dominant direction; dynamic references and external links can make the relation incomplete. Confirm/correct: Approve stages and grouping; label cross-links; disclose unresolved or runtime-only dependencies; allow one cell to appear in more than one presentation. Views — Classic: Sheet tabs, formula references; Inspector: Cross-sheet path, omitted branch count and dynamic edges; Notebook: Reading sequence can differ from calculation order; Model map: Nested sheet/stage groups with actual edges; App: Published process steps only; formulas still evaluate by workbook rules.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-08 Running balances (Loan balance carries from preceding row and subtracts principal). Evidence/limit: E for previous-row recurrence; S for a balance interpretation or its units. Confirm/correct: Confirm opening/closing terms and period axis; expose the first-row seed; do not treat a row recurrence as an iterative circular calculation. Views — Classic: 360-row Loan schedule; Inspector: Seed, previous-row relation, final balance and exceptions; Notebook: Schedule excerpt labelled `rows 1-12 of 360`; full table action; Model map: One recurrence block with initial state and period axis; App: Summary/graph plus expandable full schedule.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-09 Deliberate circular calculation (Stock's circular estimate, iteration enabled, convergence readout). Evidence/limit: E for a resolved cycle and workbook iteration settings; W for intent/convergence without evidence; unknown dependencies remain unknown. Confirm/correct: Show participating cells and settings; ask whether intended; approval annotates intent only; enabling iteration is a separate workbook-setting edit. Views — Classic: Actual circular formulas and workbook settings; Inspector: Cycle members, iteration count/residual if supplied, convergence/limit state; Notebook: Explanation plus latest actual result; no fake run button; Model map: Explicit iteration enclosure, separate from delay notation; App: Show current result and convergence warning; do not hide failure.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-10 Simulation / repeated trials (A trial table, random functions, or an existing macro/data-table sweep). Evidence/limit: E for RAND/RANDBETWEEN and data-table/macro presence; S that repeated rows are independent trials; distributions and independence are not inferred facts. Confirm/correct: Confirm trial axis, outputs and refresh trigger; show random/volatile markers; no view-side random generator, reseeding, or invented execution clock. Views — Classic: Existing trial grid/data table; Inspector: Volatility, trigger and observed run provenance; Notebook: Bound distribution chart with sample/trial counts; Model map: Trial/sweep block only when workbook mechanism is known; App: Approved controls and real trigger, visible result freshness.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-11 Control panels (Loan labelled controls; Stock reorder slider; buttons beside outputs). Evidence/limit: E for controls and linked cells; S for inferred input labels; a control can invoke a macro rather than write a value. Confirm/correct: Inspect each binding/action; approve grouping and tab order; preserve the control's actual min/max/step and linked-cell meaning. Views — Classic: Original form controls and bindings; Inspector: Control -> linked cell/macro effects; Notebook: Embedded original control or faithful alternative; Model map: Parameter port with bound control; App: Primary form/button layout; permission and disabled reason visible.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-12 Pivot summaries (Sales PivotTable, dimensions, totals and filters). Evidence/limit: E for PivotTable and cache/refresh information available in workbook; source freshness may be unknown. Confirm/correct: Choose shown dimensions; disclose refresh time/status when known; filter or refresh through the real pivot action, not a new view-only aggregate. Views — Classic: Native pivot layout and field/filter operations; Inspector: Cache/source lineage and refresh state; Notebook: Bound pivot with exact filters and totals; Model map: Pivot node between source and report; App: Approved slicers/filter controls and existing pivot results.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-13 Live data (RTD/external feed values change while the workbook is open). Evidence/limit: E for supported provider and observed updates; unavailable provider or stored result does not imply live connection. Confirm/correct: Confirm displayed source/units; show connected/stale/paused/unavailable; configure history retention as presentation; keep pause-observation distinct from stopping the feed. Views — Classic: Live cells with freshness/status cue; Inspector: Timestamped values, source state and labelled retained history; Notebook: Live result/chart, still respecting calculation mode; Model map: External-source node and actual observed updates; App: Source state next to results; no claim of currentness when stale.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-14 Macro-driven models (Inherited buttons/module and values changed by a macro). Evidence/limit: E for macro/assigned-action presence; W for effects inferred from code text; runtime observations may be partial. Confirm/correct: Show permission and platform state; record actual changed regions after a run; do not label an unexecuted macro's effects as known. Views — Classic: Workbook and real macro controls; Inspector: Permission, run boundaries and observed changes; Notebook: Bound result with last-run status; explicit macro action; Model map: Macro as action/observed-effects node, never invented dependency truth; App: Authorized macro button; plain refusal and desktop route if unavailable.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-15 Reports and dashboards (Summary KPIs, captions, charts and print areas). Evidence/limit: E for chart objects/print areas; S for report intent; merged cells and bold numbers alone are weak. Confirm/correct: Confirm reading order and source bindings; pin chart objects and outputs; keep explanatory prose separate from workbook values. Views — Classic: Original report and chart objects; Inspector: KPI -> source/formatting/data lineage; Notebook: Main reading/publishing surface; Model map: Output group, select a KPI to trace; App: Main presentation surface, authored reading order.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-16 Stocks and flows (Stock opening stock + arrivals - shipments = closing stock). Evidence/limit: E for an arithmetic relationship; S for quantity accumulation; W that every additive relationship is a physical flow. Confirm/correct: Confirm units and stock/flow roles; expose sign conventions and bounds; the diagram follows the actual formula and can be corrected independently. Views — Classic: Actual balance formulas; Inspector: Inflow/outflow/stock relationships and units; Notebook: Short explanation, bound table/chart; Model map: Main systems surface; flow role is confirmed annotation; App: Stock outputs and input controls relevant to operator.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-17 Feedback and delays (Stock reorder decisions affect later arrivals; arrows return to inventory). Evidence/limit: E for dependencies; S for feedback at a grouped level; a circular reference is not itself a time delay. Confirm/correct: Confirm lag and period axis from explicit formulas/rows; label `3 days` only with that evidence; use `iteration` for convergence loops. Views — Classic: Rows or columns implementing actual lag; Inspector: Separate dependency cycle from period lag; Notebook: Explicit lag explanation and result sequence; Model map: Labelled delayed dependency or iteration enclosure, according to evidence; App: Timing/lag explanation near outputs when it affects interpretation.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-18 Reconciliation and control totals (Inputs equal outputs; check is zero; Grand Total comparisons). Evidence/limit: E for subtraction/equality expressions; S for their role as checks; tolerance and materiality cannot be invented. Confirm/correct: Confirm check cells and what zero/TRUE means; surface existing tolerance; adding new checks or IFERROR is a separate model change. Views — Classic: Check cells and original tolerance formulas; Inspector: Failed checks grouped by affected output; no invented repairs; Notebook: Visible check summary with exact predicate; Model map: Check attached to relevant block; App: Compact checks; failure stays visible and affects readiness label.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-19 Exceptions and overrides (One hard-coded value interrupts a formula run; errors or unusual formats). Evidence/limit: E for difference from neighbouring formula structure; W that the exception is a mistake. Confirm/correct: Keep `exception` distinct from `error`; mark accepted override with an annotation; propose repair only with original/new formula and downstream preview. Views — Classic: Exact override/error cell; Inspector: Explain deviation, original neighbours and dependents; Notebook: Exception footnote linked to cell; Model map: Badge on containing block; expand precise member; App: Relevant warning, original error text and a source link.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-20 Repeated-sheet families (Similar regional/monthly sheets feed a consolidation sheet). Evidence/limit: E for matching structure/reference patterns; S for family membership; hidden sheets and local names may differ materially. Confirm/correct: Approve group, order and representative sheet; list all deviations and all members, including hidden status; never fold exceptions out of the summary. Views — Classic: All original sheets and hidden status; Inspector: Family differences and consolidation lineage; Notebook: Representative template plus all-member list; Model map: Family group with member/exception counts; App: Approved region/period chooser backed by existing workbook selection.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-21 External-file consolidation (Inherited references missing supplier or rates files). Evidence/limit: E for external-link records and resolved formulas; last stored value is not current external evidence. Confirm/correct: Map/repair a link through a workbook edit; keep `missing file`, `update not requested` and `cached result` distinct; allow read-only investigation. Views — Classic: External-link formula and stored value; Inspector: File status, known/unknown link targets and last update; Notebook: Cached-result notice and source citation; Model map: External boundary node with unresolved-edge marker; App: Visible stale/missing-source state; no optimistic `Ready`.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-22 Spill / array result (Sales FILTER result occupies changing rows; outline has one anchor). Evidence/limit: E for array/spill metadata and occupied cells; obstruction or unavailable calculation may leave shape unknown. Confirm/correct: Confirm presentation columns/labels; preserve anchor ownership; editing a spill child refuses with a jump to the anchor or obstruction. Views — Classic: Anchor/spill boundary/obstruction; Inspector: Shape, anchor, dependent ranges and error origin; Notebook: Reactive data-frame display with anchor label; Model map: Array port with dimensions or `shape unavailable`; App: Bound result table; edit requests lead to permitted inputs.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: P-23 Irregular forms and sparse layouts (Inherited contains forms, blank spacing, merged labels and separate small islands). Evidence/limit: E for cell/object geometry; S for label-to-value pairing; proximity alone is weak. Confirm/correct: Correct groups and reading order; preserve a Classic fallback; show `Unclassified content` rather than assigning a false model type. Views — Classic: Complete faithful escape hatch; Inspector: Unclassified islands, objects and formula/error inventory; Notebook: User-selected excerpts with address captions; Model map: Sheet/block overview, no forced semantic labels; App: Decline automatic publication; show `Choose inputs and outputs first`.
why: Defines recognition evidence, correction rules, and coherent five-view presentation for a recurring spreadsheet pattern.

statement: The five cast fixtures use English formula syntax (comma separators, '.' decimals), actual date values (not ambiguous strings), ZAR display formatting, and full internal calculation precision (no precision-as-displayed; round only visible text), with each storyboard starting from its stated baseline independently and formulas retaining meaning across regional locale changes.
why: Provides exact, unambiguous arithmetic baselines for prototyping and review.

statement: Budget fixture (Inputs, Monthly, Summary): Inputs!A1:C13 holds 12 Base/Stretch assumptions as an ordinary range (colours never auto-convert to an Excel Table; Stretch is not a secretly active model; unused cash/tax/debtor rows never claim operating-profit impact), Monthly B1:M11 computes 12 months (base profit 18,000/mo, Summary!B7 216,000/yr; B3=125 gives 276,000/yr with 24 changed values in Monthly!B8:M11; B3=125 & B4=72 gives 252,000/yr with 36 changed values), plus optional Budget.* names, Summary!A20 TRANSPOSE blocked by A21 note, and Summary!D14 DNA.DISCOUNT.
why: Authoritative numeric and formula specification for Budget storyboards S03-S05 and S14-S16.

statement: Sales fixture (Orders, Report, Pivot): Orders!A1:G25001 is a real 25,000-row Excel Table where West has exactly 125 Paid orders (124,250) and 1 Pending order (SO10482, data row 10482 / sheet row 10483, 4,200); Report!B5 starts at 128,450 (missing Status criterion) and repairs to 124,250, alongside XLOOKUP (B7), FILTER (A12), and an independently refresh-tracked PivotTable, with generated filler rows explicitly disclosed as synthetic.
why: Authoritative numeric and formula specification for Sales storyboards S06-S07.

statement: Loan fixture (sheet Loan): inputs B2=1,000,000, B3=10.5%, B4=360 with Stop validation (principal>0, rate 0-100%, integer months 1..360), B6=-PMT(B3/12,B4,B2) (9,147.39 at 10.5%, 10,286.13 at 12%), B7=B6*B4-B2, 360-row PMT/IPMT/PPMT schedule A12:F371 leaving rows past shorter terms blank via IF formulas (never merely hiding invalid IPMT), dynamic INDEX balance-chart ranges ending at the term, full-precision ending residual inspectable on request, and earlier-case comparison labelled as a recorded observation until explicitly saved via Excel Scenario Manager.
why: Authoritative numeric and formula specification for Loan storyboards S10-S11 and F05.

statement: Stock fixture (sheet Stock): inputs B2=400, B3=100, B4=3 (integer 1..30), B5=260 (linked to native form-control slider 0..600 step 10 and optional name Stock.ReorderPoint), B6=420, B7=20, iterative reserve B8=0.5*(B8+B7) (max 100, change 0.001, displayed 20.00 without inventing exact iterate/count), and 30-day schedule A12:H43 where day-2 order H15 (420) arrives at day-5 inflow C18 via INDEX (distinct from B8's same-period circular loop, and non-converging B8=B8+1 reports real stop reason/unavailable status rather than an invented #CYCLE! error).

statement: Inherited stress fixture (Inherited.xlsm): 40 sheets (6 hidden), ~300,000 formulas, dense Archive region, disabled VBA module LegacyClose, missing external workbook Rates2024.xlsx, Summary!F18=SUM(Revenue.Window) with deliberately stale saved value 2,401,300 vs current #REF! from broken name Revenue.Window (=OFFSET(Revenue!#REF!,0,0,12,1)), valid dynamic OFFSET names, and a recovery variant (2 committed edits + 1 unapplied draft), requiring pinned file bytes/bounds before benchmarking.
