statement: Illustrative provider DiscountFunctions.xll 1.0 defines DNA.DISCOUNT(price,rate)=price*(1-rate) for 0<=rate<=1 else #NUM! (120/0.1->108, 120/0.2->96, 120/1.2->#NUM!) and caller-dependent DNA.CALLERADDRESS() refused in standalone mode; the design does not require running native XLL binaries in a browser, but requires explicit disclosure of provider/runtime requirements, equivalent implementations, and the user's chosen host.
why: Authoritative add-in test contract for Formula Explorer storyboards S12-S13 and F06-F07.

statement: Independent arithmetic checks on Budget, Loan, Stock, and Sales confirm internal numerical consistency of the design examples only; they do not establish Excel runtime parity, native add-in loading, accessibility conformance, opening speed, or custom-XML round-trip preservation, which remain acceptance criteria in Appendices A-C.
why: Maintains strict honesty about what a design specification has and has not verified.

statement: Design provenance grounds normative requirements in 5 supplied inputs (brief, STRAND.md v0.1, LINKED_BOXES_SKIN.md's sheet-backed direction, names-in-motion.html, watershed.html), 21 primary design-evidence references (WCAG 2.2 S1/S17-S21, Excel docs S2-S4/S7-S14/S16, Pluto S5, phyphox S6, Enron corpus S15), and 33 Microsoft Classic interaction references (KA1-KA33), requiring observed pinned-Excel comparison whenever documentation is ambiguous.
why: Anchors design decisions and Classic interaction acceptance rules in primary technical sources.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Neon's self-contained HTML mockup gallery renders all 17 scenes (M-01 to M-17) with live Strand v0.2 theme switching (cockpit-light, cockpit-dark, high-contrast), workbook/section filters, WCAG AA --amber-ink (#8A5A00 / #FFD04D), dual-stroke --focus-shadow (1px petrol + 3px amber), 45-degree teal-hatched --proposal-bg Preview Seam, and 6-tone Formula Reference Palette.
why: Demonstrates Strand v0.2 token refinements and contrast compliance visually across all 17 mockups.

statement: Rejects equating 'modern' with un-Excel card walls or proprietary formula dialects: Excel's calculation semantics, file format, and addressability are the bedrock, and everything above the grid is a task-specific instrument panel.

Modernity criterion 1 (Right representation for the cognitive job): five views—Notebook (narrative + live numbers), Inspector (causal graph + anomaly probes), Model Map (blocks, wires, z⁻¹ loops), App (sliders + scenarios), and Classic (keyboard-speed grid)—project the same live .xlsx workbook.

Modernity criterion 2 (Flight-deck instrumentation instead of modal dialogs): calm petrol chrome (#193F49) holds live readouts in Mast, Bridge and Strip while the model sits unobstructed on daylight paper (#FFFFFF/#EDF1F2).

Modernity criterion 3 (Preview before commit): structural or destructive edits (fill drags, wire connections, range rewrites, AI proposals) render first across a Preview Seam with recalculated deltas, and Esc is an exact lossless revert.

Modernity criterion 4 (Human and agent parity): every object has one canonical address (Monthly!D14, Orders[Amount], Inv.OnHand, block:Monthly/Revenue) shared identically by human navigation and AI agent diffs.
Quality priority rule: Honesty > Clarity > Familiarity (in Classic) / Density (calibrated per view).

Honesty never yields: never invent non-Excel numbers, never silently truncate 304k formulas, never disguise cached missing-link values as live, never hide errors behind formatting; state simplifications or decline with a concrete way forward.
Clarity governs presentation through Strand's single block geometry, weight, tabular numerals, and semantic signals rather than competing borders, rainbow palettes, or ribbon clutter.

Familiarity governs muscle memory, not chrome artwork: Classic honours Excel keyboard/mouse choreography without Microsoft icons, ribbons, or Office-blue chrome, while other views preserve shared shell shortcuts (Ctrl+K, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Alt+1..5).

Two densities only: Working density (22 px rows, 4–6 px gaps for Classic, Inspector, Model Map, Formula Explorer) and Reading density (68 ch measure, Source Serif 4 prose for Notebook and App); no third medium mode.
Rejected alternative: an Excel-clone light-grey ribbon, because it violates the no-Microsoft-artwork rule and wastes ~110 px of vertical height needed for split diagnostics and Formula Explorer.

Rejected alternative: hiding the grid behind a modern default on every opened .xlsx, because analysts opening 40-sheet legacy files expect immediate grid footing and distrust forced graph/doc landings.

Unified four-region shell shared across views: Mast (top 36 px petrol-800: badge, file/save, View Switcher Ctrl+Alt+1..5, Lens Alt+L, Explorer Ctrl+E, Agent Ctrl+I, Palette Ctrl+K, Print, Settings, non-modal trust pills), Bridge (34 px petrol-900: Unified Address Box Ctrl+G/Alt+D, Back/Forward Alt+←/→, plus view-specific controls), Stage (14 px rounded paper: SELECTED/EDITING, dual-stroke amber ring, 150 ms Continuity Halo, Preview Seam, Alt+Hover peek), and Strip (bottom 26 px petrol-800: sheet tabs with view micro-glyphs, Calc State, clickable Error Counter Pill, aggregates, Density, Semantic Zoom).

Strand v0.2 refinement 1 (amber contrast fix): raw #FFB301 on white fails WCAG AA (~1.84:1), so add --dna-amber-ink (#8A5A00 light ~5.7:1; #FFD04D dark ~12.4:1) for amber text/badges and render light-paper focus outlines as a dual-stroke ring (2 px #FFB301 outer + 1 px #193F49 inner keyline).
why: Passes WCAG AA contrast while keeping amber the sole saturated attention channel.

statement: Strand v0.2 refinement 2 (Preview Seam & Agent grammar without adding a hue): uncommitted AI proposals use a dashed teal-600 border over an 8% petrol-teal 45-degree hairline hatch (--dna-proposal-bg) with [⇄ Agent] badge, settling with a 150 ms green-500 fresh pulse on accept.

Strand v0.2 refinement 3 (editing-only Formula Reference Palette): adds 6 WCAG-checked accents (teal-ink, prov-const, green-ink, amber-ink, slate-ink #4A5D7A, plum-ink #6E4775—excluding error red #D02A23) paired with circled numbers ①②③④ matching Formula Bar superscripts, active only during editing or tracing.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand v0.2 refinement 4 (Themes vs Skins): three Strand themes remain the canonical baseline while declarative Skins may override non-semantic tokens and arrange panels, checked by an automated Strand Contrast & Safety Gate blocking WCAG AA failures or repurposing of red/signal.

Strand v0.2 refinement 5 (Model Map preview harmonisation): ports directors, z⁻¹ delay chips, inline FSM diagrams, event queues and fan charts from names-in-motion/watershed into Strand's palette with dashed-double-stroke + ↻ badge for circular iteration blocks (zero extra hues).

Strand v0.2 refinement 6 (Instrument Overlay Layer in Classic): renders author Excel formatting faithfully on paper while placing DNA Calc structural signals (provenance micro-ticks, volatile corners, error triangles, selection halo) on a non-destructive overlay toggled via Ctrl+Shift+P.

Principle 1 (Excel Truth Over Visual Tidiness): expose exact Excel oddities (blank-to-0 coercion, OFFSET volatility, 1900 leap-year dates, range truncation) and explain them plainly rather than smoothing over them silently.

Principle 2 (Infer First, Declare Never Unless Correcting): every view delivers an honest first view on any plain .xlsx immediately without upfront schemas, persisting user/agent corrections quietly in customXml.

Principle 3 (Same Address, Continuous Place): switching views, opening Formula Explorer, or stepping agent diffs preserves anchor focus centered with a 150 ms Continuity Halo; Esc unwinds strictly one layer (Editing → Selected → Drawer Closed).

Principle 4 (Never Trap, Never Block, Never Hang): no modal security walls on open, no frozen scrollbars during 300k-formula indexing, and no dead-end App screens lacking a path back to the model (unless Excel sheet protection is set).

First paint of Inherited.xlsx (M-01): paints cached active sheet values in 180 ms (<220 ms) with zero blocking popups, docks a single non-modal Trust & Triage Banner (40 sheets / 6 hidden, 304k formulas, 47 errors / 4 roots, 3 missing links, 1 blocked macro modRollForward, 9 volatile OFFSET names), streams background dependency indexing in the Strip, marks unresolved external links with signal-orange ▸ ticks and errors with red left hairlines + ⊗ icons, exposes [+6 hidden ▾] without unhiding, and announces summary to screen readers.

Inspector on Inherited.xlsx (Ctrl+Alt+2, <60 ms, M-02) preserves Exec_Summary!D9 focus with 150 ms Continuity Halo, renders 40 sheets as a 4-tier Workbook Atlas (L0 Atlas) with dashed [hidden]/[veryHidden] tags, collapses 47 errors into 4 root causes with read-only fuzzy key hints ('NP15_Peak' vs 'NP15_PK'), and lists 9 volatile OFFSET names (142k downstream cells) with a non-destructive INDEX/Table tip.

Honest Model Map refusal on Dispatch_Hourly (M-03, 45 ms): declines rendering 182,400 cell boxes and displays a Scale Notice Banner confirming 100% coverage across 12 exact R1C1 formula-pattern runs (0 cells omitted), each with range span, shared formula, aggregates over all 8,760 rows, surfaced interior #DIV/0! jumps back to Classic, and Ctrl+Shift+C Markdown health summary export.

First visit to Notebook (Ctrl+Alt+3) presents a First-Run Scaffold Card choosing between 'Draft from Workbook Structure' (70 ms, Reading density 68 ch Source Serif 4, linked live without duplicating formulas) and 'Start Blank Notebook'.

Budget Notebook write-up (M-04): prose supports '=' / Ctrl+Shift+R inline Live Value Chips («$2,889,851») updating in <12 ms with 140 ms green pulse when toggling the inline Scenario Control (Inputs!C2); pasting Classic ranges creates a Linked Live Data Frame with a 5 s Paste Options chip (Ctrl); inline /calc formula blocks allocate a real backed Excel cell and defined name (Summary!B19 Cash_Runway_Gain) with no floating non-Excel math; Alt+P toggles Vertical ↔ Pipeline.

Notebook cross-view undo, export and accessibility: Ctrl+Z in Classic reverts edits made in Notebook with a Strip toast naming origin, Ctrl+S persists prose/layout in customXml, Ctrl+C exports resolved rich HTML + Markdown + SVG charts to email/Word, 200% zoom reflows prose cleanly, and live chips expose descriptive ARIA labels.

Sales discrepancy audit in Inspector (M-05, <50 ms): Formula Lens (Alt+L) structures SUMIFS as readable LET with live argument chips and row-count flags; Structural Anomaly Probe catches hardcoded Orders!$K$2:$K$20000 stopping 5,001 rows short of 25,000-row Table Orders, computes the exact excluded EMEA/Q3 slice (493 rows = $118,420.00 matching Pivot variance D14), maps downstream corruption (Rebate Tier F8 and Rebate G8), and offers a speculative Preview Fix to structured table refs.

Inspecting excluded rows jumps to Classic with a non-destructive diagnostic highlight (leaving Excel AutoFilter untouched); applying the structured-ref fix detects and offers to fix 3 matching sibling cells (Report!D6:D9) as one atomic Undo step (18 ms recalc), copies Markdown audit trace, and supports full keyboard graph traversal and aria-live announcements.

Model Map empty state offers starter actions (I Input Box, B Calc/State Box, G Group Frame, S Form Control Slider) noting every box writes standard Excel defined names on a visible sheet; port-to-port wiring (mouse drag or W key) rewrites real backing formulas through the AST Formula-Name Interpreter, and pasting vectors onto a box previews dynamic array spills.

Circular feedback Preview Seam on Model Map (M-06): self-wiring Inv.OnHand while Iterative Calculation is OFF pauses with an inline popover offering [Enable Iteration: 1 pass/tick (Ticks Director)], [Custom Iteration Settings…], or [Esc: Cancel Wire]; enabling updates standard Excel Iterative/MaxIterations/MaxChange properties, renders a dashed z⁻¹ delay loop and Ticks Director bar (▶ Run, Step F9, Reset), and S adds a genuine OOXML Form Control slider mirrored in the Parameter Rail.

Running ticks animates a 140 ms amber topological recalc ripple (instant highlights under reduced motion); switching to Classic (Ctrl+Alt+1, M-07) centers Inv.OnHand (StockModel!B18) with Continuity Halo, standard Excel formula, OOXML Form Control slider over D8:F8, teal spill border on B10:D10, and ↻ Iter overlay pill, with atomic cross-view Ctrl+Z undo and full keyboard graph navigation.

Unified Address Grammar covers seven entity kinds: Cell (Sheet!A1), Range (Sheet!A1:D12), Block (block:Sheet/BlockId), Name (Inv.OnHand), Table (Orders[Amount]), Object (obj:Sheet/ObjectName), and View Item (view:ViewId/ItemId, customXml only); View Items always carry a dotted focus frame and [View] tag so they are never mistaken for cells.

Non-grid edit mapping table: every non-grid gesture maps deterministically to plain Excel mutations (AST wire rewrite, slider cell write, assumption write, backed /calc cell+name allocation, Inspector structured-ref fix) or presentation-only customXml updates (prose, card order, box coordinates); Formula-Name Presenter/Interpreter operates strictly on parsed AST.

One chronological dual-tagged ([Model] / [View]) Undo/Redo stack per workbook spans all views; Ctrl+Z undoes the latest action without view whiplash (showing a Strip toast with [Jump]), Ctrl+Shift+Z peeks/filters history, and both model and customXml deltas journal continuously for non-modal crash recovery.

Visible state taxonomy: Errors distinguish Root Origin (filled ⊗) vs Propagated (hollow ⊘) in red-ink; Strip reports exact calc state (✓ Clean, ⚠ Dirty Manual [F9], ◐ Calculating % Esc-abortable, ↻ Iterative Converged vs Max-Reached Unconverged); RTD/external/async/volatile cells show signal-orange ▸ ticks with freshness hover and UI-side RTD throttle.

Formula Lens (Alt+L across every view) substitutes defined names/Table headers, structures nested expressions into indented LET bindings with inline evaluated chips, and strips group prefixes; always displays '[Readable view · Hover/Alt for raw Excel]' and never alters stored formulas unless the user explicitly invokes 'Refactor cell to real LET in workbook'.

Non-blocking Pattern Inference Pass combines six verifiable Excel signals—grid geometry/OOXML objects, R1C1 formula signatures, cell provenance, dependency graph topology, number-format axes, and defined names/Data Validation—without brittle regex over labels.

Three calibrated confidence tiers: High (≥0.85, OOXML objects or unambiguous R1C1 structure, auto-applied), Medium (0.50–0.84, dashed 'Inferred · [Confirm / Change]' badge), and Low (<0.50, kept strictly as raw grid/cells—never fabricated into false abstraction).
Two-click human or agent block classification popover (Reclassify, Adjust Range, Merge/Split, Dismiss Inference) persists overrides in customXml so Excel preserves them and DNA Calc never asks twice.

Neon organises 18 recurring patterns into 5 families (Data & Reference, Parameters & Controls, Calculation Engines, State/Feedback/Stochastic, Governance/Automation/Presentation), adding three critical real-world patterns: #16 Reconciliations & check blocks, #17 Dynamic array / SPILL pipelines & LAMBDA libraries, and #18 External-link consolidation & staging hubs.
Inherited.xlsx (40 sheets, 6 hidden, 304,218 formulas, Dispatch_Hourly A1:CZ8760, 3 missing links, 1 VBA module, 9 OFFSET names, 47 errors) is the Show/Simplify/Decline stress benchmark.

Classic scaling policy — Shows all: Always renders the full virtualized grid (up to Excel's 1,048,576 × 16,384 bounds) on demand. Simplifies: When zoomed out `< 55%` (Semantic Zoom), swaps tiny cell text for **L1/L2 Block Headers** (`Dispatch_Hourly · 8,760 rows · ⊗5`); zooming back in restores every cell. Declines: Never declines—Classic is always the universal bedrock.

Inspector scaling policy — Shows all: Shows all 40 sheets (including hidden/very-hidden), all 4 error root causes, all 3 missing links, all 9 `OFFSET` names, and full trace of any selected cell. Simplifies: Collapses 47 errors to 4 root causes (expandable to all 47); collapses `Dispatch_Hourly`'s 182,400 cells into **12 R1C1 formula runs** inside the Workbook Atlas (`L0`) and Calc Order waves. Declines: Never declines; if a single cell has `> 500` direct precedents (e.g., `SUM` over 8,760 rows), shows the range as **one bounded range node** (`K2:K8761 · 8,760 cells`) with expand-on-demand instead of 8,760 arrows.

Model Map scaling policy — Shows all: Shows all nodes/wires when active scope has `≤ 120` actors/blocks (e.g., `Stock`, `Budget`, `Sales!Report`). Simplifies: For `121–2,000` cells or large uniform sheets (`Dispatch_Hourly`), automatically folds contiguous identical R1C1 formulas into **Formula-Pattern Runs** (12 runs = 100% of 182,400 formulas) with a persistent top Scale Notice (`M-03`), min/max/sum across all rows, and row-sample badge. Declines: **Declines cell-level graph** for `> 120` non-foldable bespoke cells on a single canvas or raw 25k-row database tables (`Orders`), displaying: *"Too dense for cell-level wiring (182,400 formulas). Showing 12 exact formula runs (100% covered) — or [Open in Inspector] / [Jump to Classic]."*

Notebook scaling policy — Shows all: Shows all curated prose, inputs, charts, and summary tables (`≤ 200` rows rendered directly). Simplifies: Large linked ranges or tables (`Orders` 25,000 rows) display as **Sampled Data Frames** showing the first 200 rows + full-table aggregates (`Sum/Avg/Count over all 25,000 rows`) with an unmistakable footer notice (`Showing 200 of 25,000 rows · Aggregates exact over all rows · [Inspect Full Table]`). Declines: **Declines auto-scaffolding** all 40 sheets of `Inherited` at once; presents a sheet picker pre-selecting `Exec_Summary` (*"40 sheets detected — pick which sheets to include in this Notebook"*).

App scaling policy — Shows all: Works whenever a clean Input/Output contract exists (explicit skin or high-confidence inference). Simplifies: Groups schedules `> 50` rows automatically by Year/Category (`Loan`'s 360 months → 30 expandable annual rows) with explicit count disclosure. Declines: **Declines auto-generation** on `Inherited`: *"This workbook has 40 sheets, 47 unresolved errors, and no clear input/output block. Triage in Inspector [Ctrl+Alt+2] or build an explicit App skin first."*

Formula Explorer scaling policy — Shows all: Always evaluates and displays the complete AST of any single formula. Simplifies: Array arguments `> 50` elements render as scrollable virtualized previews with explicit dimensions (`8,760 × 1 array · showing 1..20 · [Inspect All]`). Declines: Never declines a valid Excel formula.

Five honest simplification techniques: (1) named blocks with exact A1 bounds, (2) R1C1 formula-run folding always surfacing interior exceptions/errors, (3) L0→L3 Semantic Zoom keeping text ≥11 px, (4) local expand-on-demand, and (5) sampled previews stating exact row counts while computing aggregates over 100% of rows.

Performance budget (**File open → Interactive Cached First Paint** (`Inherited`, 304k formulas)): Desktop `≤ 250 ms`, Browser `≤ 450 ms`. Ceiling/fallback: Cached values paint immediately; dependency indexing streams off main thread with Strip progress.

Performance budget (**Keystroke echo** (typing in cell / Formula Bar / Notebook)): Desktop `≤ 12 ms` (1 frame @ 60–120 Hz), Browser `≤ 16 ms`. Ceiling/fallback: Input buffer never waits on recalculation or inference.

Performance budget (**Grid arrow navigation / smooth scroll** (60 fps)): Desktop `≤ 8 ms / frame`, Browser `≤ 16 ms / frame`. Ceiling/fallback: Strict viewport virtualization; zero DOM nodes for off-screen cells.

Performance budget (**View switch** (`Ctrl+Alt+1..5`, preserving anchor)): Desktop `≤ 60 ms`, Browser `≤ 100 ms`. Ceiling/fallback: Target view paints skeleton/cached layout within 1 frame if heavy layout runs async.

Performance budget (**Interactive edit → Recalc feedback** (`Budget`/`Loan`/`Stock` < 5k cells)): Desktop `≤ 16 ms`, Browser `≤ 30 ms`. Ceiling/fallback: Instantaneous; no spinner ever flashes for `< 150 ms` work.

Performance budget (**Heavy recalc progress indicator** (`Inherited` 304k formulas, volatile `OFFSET`)): Desktop Progress pill appears at `150 ms`; UI remains scrollable/cancelable (`Esc`), Browser Same (`150 ms` threshold). Ceiling/fallback: Never freezes the main thread; stale cells subtly dim with `◐ Calculating…` in Strip.

Three never-acceptable failure modes: never hang UI thread (>150 ms work runs off-thread with Strip progress and Esc abort), never silently drop content (always show exact coverage counts), and never misstate the model (mark cached missing links ▸, manual dirty cells, unconverged iterations, and run exceptions).

Honesty/parity: Discloses active scenario parameters and print timestamp; never drops schedule rows silently.

Each storyboard runs as a 15-minute moderated usability test on desktop and browser including keyboard-only and screen-reader variants.

Usability script UT-1 (Analyst · `Inherited.xlsx`): *"You just inherited this file. Without editing it yet, tell me how many independent root problems exist, why it feels slow, and inspect `Dispatch_Hourly`."* — Criteria: Reaches first paint `< 300 ms` with zero modal blocks; identifies all **4 root causes**, **3 missing links**, and **9 `OFFSET` names** in `≤ 3 min`; understands Model Map's 12-run summary without thinking rows were deleted.

Usability script UT-2 (Analyst · `Budget.xlsx`): *"Turn this budget into a 1-page live memo for your director with live Revenue/EBITDA figures and a Stretch toggle, then copy the summary into email."* — Criteria: Creates Notebook draft, binds `≥ 2` live prose chips, toggles `Base ↔ Stretch` verifying live update, pastes a linked Classic range, and undoes an input edit from Classic cleanly (`≤ 6 min`, `≤ 1` prompt hint).

Usability script UT-3 (Auditor · `Sales.xlsx`): *"Q3 EMEA on `Report` doesn't match the PivotTable. Find out why, confirm what else is wrong downstream, and fix it cleanly."* — Criteria: Pinpoints hardcoded `$20000` ceiling + 493 excluded rows (`$118,420`) and downstream Rebate Tier error (`F8/G8`) in `≤ 4 min`; applies structured-ref fix reducing `D14` to `$0`; verifies `Ctrl+Z` revert.

Usability script UT-4 (Systems Eng. · `Stock.xlsx`): *"Build an inventory loop with 3-day reorder delay and a ReorderPoint slider on Model Map, run 10 ticks, then verify Excel parity in Classic."* — Criteria: Wires boxes without help; resolves circular-ref Preview Seam in 1 click (enabling Iteration); runs ticks seeing topological ripple; locates exact formula & Form Slider in Classic (`≤ 8 min`).

Usability script UT-5 (Manager · `Loan.xlsx`): *"Compare paying `$300` extra per month against the Base loan, try typing an invalid `-2%` rate to see what happens, and export a 2-page PDF."* — Criteria: Zero accidental formula edits; recovers from `-2%` validation refusal in `< 5 s`; creates side-by-side comparison discovering `$142,795` interest savings; prints clean 2-page brief (`≤ 4 min`).

Usability script UT-6 (Add-in Dev · Standalone + `Budget`): *"Load `TaxPack.xll` with no workbook open, diagnose why `TAX.EFFRATE(290311,"CA",TRUE)` fails, verify `0.00%` formatting, then test and commit it in `Budget!Summary!B13`."* — Criteria: Loads unsigned add-in via sandbox prompt; catches `"US-CA"` arg error via Eval Tree in `< 90 s`; verifies preview deltas (`-$20,276` Net Income) in Classic before committing (`≤ 5 min`).

Usability script UT-7 (Analyst + Agent · `Budget.xlsx`): *"Ask the agent for +5% Q3 pricing and 15% Marketing. Review impact in both Classic and Notebook, keep pricing, reject or undo Marketing."* — Criteria: Reviews staged Preview Seam across both views without premature commit; accepts Hunk 1 cleanly; reverts Hunk 2 via Reject or single `Ctrl+Z`; locates both actions in Audit Log (`≤ 4 min`).

Usability script UT-8 (Keyboard / SR Audit · All 5): *"Execute UT-1, UT-3, UT-4 (wire with `W`), and UT-5 using keyboard + screen reader only at 200% zoom and `high-contrast` theme."* — Criteria: 100% task completion with zero keyboard traps, zero unlabeled icons, accurate `aria-live` recalc announcements, zero WCAG AA contrast failures.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Push-back: forbid executable custom widget code inside .xlsx skins because it creates a second macro-security hole; keep workbook-embedded customXml skins 100% declarative and restrict coded widgets to signed, user-installed extensions with declarative fallback.

Risk (High severity): **Classic muscle-memory regressions** (one broken `F4`, `Ctrl+Enter`, or double-click fill gesture loses Excel power users permanently) Mitigation: Treat **Appendix A** as a blocking automated conformance suite (every gesture tested in CI on desktop + browser before Classic exits beta).

Risk (High severity): **Browser keyboard shortcut hijacking** (`Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+T`, `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+1..5`, `Alt` menus intercepted by Chrome/Edge/Safari) Mitigation: Full native capture on desktop + installed PWA (`Keyboard Lock API` where supported); deterministic documented fallback chords (`Alt+Shift+1..5` / `Ctrl+K` palette) surfaced dynamically in browser tooltips.

Risk (Medium severity): **False-positive pattern inference on Enron-style messes** (`Inherited`) misclassifying interleaved legacy sheets Mitigation: Strict confidence gating (`< 0.50` stays raw grid), zero silent mutations, one-click `[Dismiss / Reclassify]` persisted in `customXml`.

Risk (Medium severity): **Round-trip stripping of `customXml` by third-party tools** (Excel preserves `customXml`, but LibreOffice/Google Sheets/some ETL libraries may drop unknown parts) Mitigation: Keep every workbook 100% self-sufficient without `customXml` (auto-inference regenerates sensible Notebook/Inspector/Map views on open); warn cleanly if a reopened file lost its saved skin part.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API

C-1 (Immediate Cached Snapshot): On workbook open, supply sheet metadata (including hidden/very-hidden state), formatting, and cached cell values for the visible viewport before full dependency graph construction or recalculation finishes.

C-2 (Progressive Off-Thread Indexing & Recalc Progress): Report incremental progress counts (`completed / total formulas`) and support safe cancellation (`Esc`) during long indexing or recalculation passes without blocking UI reads.

C-3 (Excel-Preserved Extension Part Read/Write): Read and write arbitrary XML/JSON view, layout, prose, inference-override, and declarative-skin payloads inside an `.xlsx` extension part (`customXml`) that Microsoft Excel preserves untouched across save cycles, and detect if an external editor stripped that part on reopen.
C-4 (Crash Recovery Delta Stream): Provide lightweight read/write access to incremental local recovery snapshots of uncommitted model and presentation edits.

C-5 (Changed-Cell & Changed-Name Diffs): After every recalculation, return the exact list of changed cells and defined names along with their previous and new values (and error states) so views can highlight deltas and animate ripples.

C-6 (Speculative / Transactional Preview Calculation): Evaluate a proposed set of cell, formula, name, or calc-setting edits in an isolated speculative overlay (without committing them to the live workbook) and return full downstream recalculated values, error introductions, and affected-cell counts—powering the Preview Seam for Formula Explorer, Inspector fixes, circular-ref previews, and AI Agent Proposal Batches.

C-7 (Exact Calc State & Convergence Telemetry): Expose workbook calculation mode (`Automatic`, `Automatic Except Data Tables`, `Manual`), dirty state, last recalc duration, per-block recalc timings, Excel iterative calculation settings (`Iterative`, `MaxIterations`, `MaxChange`), and whether the latest iterative solve converged or hit the iteration cap (with final residual delta).

C-8 (Manual / Scoped Recalculation Triggers): Support invoking standard Excel recalculation scopes (`F9` dirty all, `Shift+F9` active sheet, `Ctrl+Alt+F9` full, `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F9` rebuild graph + full).

C-9 (Partial & Standalone Expression Evaluation): Evaluate any arbitrary formula string or highlighted sub-expression against either a live cell's workbook context (`F9` inline / embedded Formula Explorer) or a caller-supplied dictionary of local scalar/array/error inputs with **no workbook loaded** (standalone Formula Explorer), returning a step-by-step evaluated AST tree with exact Excel types and coercions.

C-10 (Parsed Formula AST & Rewrite Support): Provide the parsed formula syntax tree with exact character spans for every token (functions, cell/range refs, structured table refs, defined names, strings, operators) and lossless AST-to-Excel-string serialization—powering numbered range highlighting, `F4` anchor cycling, Formula Lens `LET`/name presentation, and the Linked-Boxes Presenter/Interpreter.

C-11 (Cell-, Range-, Block-, and Name-Level Precedents & Dependents): Query direct and transitive precedents and dependents not only as flattened cell coordinates, but preserving **defined-name edges**, **structured table references**, and **dynamic references** (`OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`, `INDEX`), plus summarized block/sheet-level edges for 300k-formula workbooks.

C-12 (Topological Evaluation Waves): Return a topological ordering (evaluation waves) over active blocks/names/sheets, explicitly identifying strongly connected components (circular cycles and self-loops).

C-13 (Root-Cause vs Propagated Error Classification): Classify every error cell in the workbook as either a Root Origin or Propagated from specific upstream root cell(s), grouped with exact affected downstream counts.

C-14 (R1C1 Formula-Run Clustering & Exception Detection): Group contiguous cells sharing identical R1C1 formula patterns into compact runs (`F2:K8761`, 52,560 cells), while explicitly surfacing any outlier cells (hardcoded overrides, mismatched formulas, errors) within or adjacent to a run.

C-15 (Structural Anomaly Queries): Detect and report Excel-valid structural hazards on demand: hardcoded range references partially covering an Excel Table (`Sales!Report!D8`), volatile functions (`OFFSET`/`INDIRECT`/`NOW`/`RAND`) with their downstream fan-out counts, inconsistent row/column formulas, and lookup misses with nearest-match diagnostics.

C-16 (Pattern Inference Metadata Feed): Expose sheet structure primitives needed for pattern inference: contiguous region bounds, Excel Tables (`ListObject` columns/totals), PivotTables & cache sources, Data Tables (`=TABLE(...)`), Form Controls and their linked cells, Charts and series ranges, Data Validation rules, and dynamic array spill footprints.
C-17 (Number Format Engine): Format any numeric, date, text, or error value against any Excel format code and locale—both for grid rendering and live testing in Formula Explorer's Number Format Lab.

C-18 (Conditional Formatting Evaluation & Rule Inspection): Evaluate which Conditional Formatting rules trigger for any cell (or for an arbitrary override test value in Formula Explorer's CF Simulator) and return resolved styles and `Stop If True` outcomes.

C-19 (Data Validation Query & Check): Inspect Excel Data Validation rules on any cell and validate candidate user inputs before commit, returning structured rule descriptions for inline refusal messages (`App`, `Notebook`, `Classic`).

C-20 (Excel-Exact Structural Edit Primitives): Execute atomic workbook operations with full Excel reference updating: fill series / double-click fill extent calculation, drag-move / cut-paste reference relocation, insert/delete rows/columns/cells with shift, copy-with-relative-shift, `Ctrl+Enter` batch commit, and atomic multi-cell transaction commit/rollback for Unified Undo.
C-21 (External Link Inventory & Cache Provenance): List all external workbook links, their resolution status (resolved vs missing), last-cached values, and every cell depending on them.

C-22 (Live RTD / Async Feed Events & Throttling): Expose active RTD topics and async add-in cells with per-topic update timestamps, event frequencies, and a UI-side visual pause/throttle hook that never alters formula definitions.

C-23 (Add-in Registry, Sandbox Loading & Diagnostics): Load/reload add-ins (`.xll`, JS/WASM) with explicit signature/trust metadata, enumerate registered custom functions with parameter docs, tag dependent cells with add-in provenance, and return rich per-argument error diagnostics from add-in calls when available.

C-24 (Macro Quarantine & Read-Only Code Inspection): Detect VBA/macro modules on open without executing them, allow read-only source inspection, gate execution behind explicit user session trust, and relay standard Excel object-model UI events (`Activate`, `Select`) plus optional safe View API calls to the front end.
C-25 (Excel Print Metadata): Expose sheet Print Area, page breaks, margins, scaling, repeat rows/columns, and header/footer definitions for faithful Classic printing.

C-26 (Vector Chart & PivotTable Data Bindings): Provide live series data, axes, titles, and formatting metadata for Excel Charts and PivotTable layout/totals so Notebook, App, Model Map, and Print Preview can render crisp vector visuals synchronized with recalculation.

C-27 (Unified Entity Resolution & Address Formatter): Resolve any canonical address (`Sheet!A1`, `Name`, `Table[Col]`, `block:...`, `obj:...`) to its backing cells/metadata and generate canonical addresses in either A1 or R1C1 notation.
C-28 (Workbook-Safe Name Allocation): When Notebook or Model Map creates a new named calculation, allocate a non-colliding cell location and valid Excel defined name cleanly.

C-29 (Read-Only Snapshot Access for Agents): Provide an AI agent read-only access to the workbook's structure, inferred patterns, formulas, values, and diagnostics via the same Unified Address Grammar without blocking user interaction.

C-30 (Agent Proposal Diff & Audit Metadata): Validate proposed agent edits against Excel syntax, sheet protection, and speculative recalculation (C-6), returning per-hunk diffs and error checks prior to commit.

C-31 (Virtualized Window Reads): Read visible rectangular slices of cells, styles, and overlays (`25,000+` or `8,760 × 104` sheets) in constant time relative to viewport size, never requiring full-sheet materialization in UI memory.

C-32 (Fast Filtered Row Slicing Without Mutating Sheet State): Query matching rows of a Table or range (e.g., `Orders!20001:25001` matching `Region="EMEA"` and `Quarter="Q3"` in Inspector) for read-only inspection without altering the workbook's AutoFilter state.

Pattern **1. Sheet-as-database** (`Sales!Orders`, 25,000 rows): Human sees: Flat header row with uniform typed columns, thousands of record rows, few or zero cross-row formulas; read by `SUMIFS`/`XLOOKUP`/Pivot. DNA Calc recognises: Excel `ListObject` Table (**High 0.98**) or contiguous `≥ 50` uniform typed rows with unique header row & fan-out lookups (**High 0.88**). Confirm/correct: Click inferred Table/DB chip → `[Confirm DB]`, `[Adjust Header/Range]`, or `[Convert to Excel Table Ctrl+T]`. Views: **Classic:** Full virtualized grid + sticky headers + AutoFilter. **Inspector:** Single source node `[Table: Orders · 25k]`, checks partial-range refs. **Notebook:** Sampled 200-row Data Frame with visible count notice + full-table stats. **Model Map:** Single compact database source block (never 25k boxes). **App:** Read-only searchable/filtered lookup or hidden backing data.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **2. Inputs & assumptions** (`Budget!Inputs`, `Loan!C3:C7`): Human sees: Dedicated sheet/top block of labeled constants (often blue text or shaded fill), zero precedents, high fan-out to formula blocks. DNA Calc recognises: Zero-precedent constant cells adjacent to text labels with `≥ 2` downstream formula dependents (**High 0.88** when on dedicated sheet/named; **Medium 0.72** inline). Confirm/correct: Click block frame → `[Mark as Inputs]`, exclude/include cells, or bind widget type (`slider`, `percent`) in `customXml`. Views: **Classic:** `prov-const` (`#2D6A8A`) provenance ticks in overlay; author fills intact. **Inspector:** Tier-0 source cluster in Atlas; sensitivity fan-out count. **Notebook:** Editable assumption card strip (`M-04`). **Model Map:** Left-edge parameter boxes + right Parameter Rail. **App:** Primary validated left-rail form controls.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **3. Calculation blocks** (`Budget!Monthly` Rev/Cost, `Inherited!Dispatch_Hourly`): Human sees: Rectangular labeled sections with uniform copied formulas down/across and a subtotal/total row at the bottom or right. DNA Calc recognises: Contiguous region of identical R1C1 formula patterns bounded by blank rows/headers and/or `SUM`/`SUBTOTAL` footer (**High 0.90**; **Medium 0.70** if mixed overrides). Confirm/correct: Click block border to merge/split sections, rename block, or flag intentional overrides vs anomalies. Views: **Classic:** Native grid + optional Provenance Overlay flagging formula outliers. **Inspector:** Folded formula-run node showing timing & exceptions. **Notebook:** Linked Data Frame with formula peek on hover. **Model Map:** Single Calc Box or Composite (`L2 Formula Runs` when huge). **App:** Hidden engine or summarized readout table.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **4. Time series with periods across** (`Budget!Monthly!B4:N15`): Human sees: Columns labeled `Jan–Dec`, `Q1–Q4`, or `2026–2030` across top; metrics down left; horizontal roll-forward (`=B5*(1+g)`) + right-edge `Total`. DNA Calc recognises: Sequential date/period header axis (`≥ 3` columns) with uniform horizontal R1C1 recurrence + optional right-edge `SUM` column (**High 0.92**). Confirm/correct: Confirm period axis (`Monthly`/`Quarterly`) or adjust total column inclusion in block popover. Views: **Classic:** Frozen row/col panes + horizontal scroll. **Inspector:** Single time-series run with recurrence arrow (`t-1 → t`). **Notebook:** Compact Data Frame + auto-offered inline sparkline & FY Total (`M-04`). **Model Map:** Period-folded vector box showing trend sparkline & end-period value. **App:** Line/bar chart + collapsible annual/quarterly summary table.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **5. Scenarios & sensitivity tables** (`Budget!Inputs` Base/Stretch, `watershed` `=TABLE`): Human sees: Parallel scenario columns (`Base`/`Stretch`) with an active switch (`IF`/`CHOOSE`/`INDEX`), or Excel 1D/2D Data Table (`{=TABLE(r,c)}`). DNA Calc recognises: `{=TABLE(...)}` AST node (**High 0.99**); active selector cell with Data Validation list feeding `IF`/`CHOOSE`/`INDEX` across parallel columns (**High 0.86**; **Medium 0.68** without DV). Confirm/correct: Confirm scenario names, selector cell address, or add custom preset snapshots in `customXml`. Views: **Classic:** Native Data Table / scenario columns; Strip notes manual-table recalc mode if set. **Inspector:** Shows sweep dimensions & recalc cost (e.g., `25 × 52 runs`). **Notebook:** Interactive scenario toggle strip (`● Base
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **6. Reference / lookup tables** (`Inherited!Curve_Lookup`, `Sales!Report!H5:K8`): Human sees: Small-to-medium key→value mapping table (rates, tiers, FX, curves) targeted by `XLOOKUP`, `VLOOKUP`, `INDEX/MATCH`. DNA Calc recognises: Contiguous key+value block targeted as lookup array by `≥ 1` `XLOOKUP`/`VLOOKUP`/`MATCH` formula (**High 0.91**). Confirm/correct: Confirm key column and whether approximate (`-1`/`1`) or exact (`0`) matching is expected. Views: **Classic:** Grid with lookup-key highlight on hover in Provenance Overlay. **Inspector:** Lookup hub node showing miss counts & nearest-key fuzzy hints (`M-02`). **Notebook:** Collapsible appendix reference block. **Model Map:** Compact lookup table actor feeding dependent calc boxes. **App:** Hidden backing table (or read-only rate card modal).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **7. Pipelines across sheets** (`Budget`: `Inputs → Monthly → Summary`, `Inherited` 40 sheets): Human sees: Data flows left-to-right across tabs (`Raw → Staging → Calc → Report`) with minimal reverse cross-sheet references. DNA Calc recognises: Directed acyclic graph (DAG) of inter-sheet cell/name edges computed from dependency graph (**High 0.96**). Confirm/correct: Confirm/reorder logical stage tiers or group sheets into domain clusters in Atlas/Map. Views: **Classic:** Sheet tabs with subtle flow tooltip on hover; `Ctrl+[`/`]` jumps across sheets. **Inspector:** Tiered **Workbook Atlas** (`L0`) showing inter-sheet edge counts & bottlenecks (`M-02`). **Notebook:** Horizontal **Pipeline Mode** (`Alt+P`, `M-14`) mirroring sheet flow. **Model Map:** Top-level Composite boxes wired left-to-right (`Stock`, `Dam`). **App:** Collapses intermediate sheets; exposes only inputs and final outputs.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **8. Running balances & deliberate circular references** (`Loan` balance, `Stock!Inv.OnHand`, `watershed` Finance): Human sees: Row-by-row accumulator (`=PrevBal - Principal`), or intentional interest/cash/inventory self-loop with Iterative Calc enabled. DNA Calc recognises: Vertical lag formula (`R[-1]C`) over monotonically indexed axis (**High 0.94**); strongly connected component / self-loop in dependency graph (**High 0.99**). Confirm/correct: Confirm intentional circular loop vs accidental bug; adjust `MaxIterations` / `MaxChange` via Preview Seam (`M-06`). Views: **Classic:** Grid + `↻ Iter` overlay pill + Strip convergence readout (`Converged` vs `Max Iter Reached`). **Inspector:** Highlights cycle strongly-connected component & convergence delta trace. **Notebook:** Summary opening/ending balance + chart + expandable period ledger. **Model Map:** Dashed feedback loop with `z⁻¹` delay chip or `Iteration` director badge (`M-15`). **App:** Trajectory chart + grouped balance summary (`M-16`).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **9. Simulations** (`watershed` 25 rainfall futures, Monte Carlo `RAND`/`NORM.INV`): Human sees: Stochastic formulas (`RAND`, `NORM.INV`) paired with Data Table sweeps or repeated scenario runs producing percentiles (`P10`/`P50`/`P90`). DNA Calc recognises: Presence of volatile RNG functions (`RAND`/`RANDBETWEEN`) feeding `{=TABLE(...)}` or percentile aggregations (**High 0.90**; **Medium 0.65** for single-cell `RAND`). Confirm/correct: Confirm trial count, seed cell, and output distribution metrics; pause auto-recalc on edit if desired. Views: **Classic:** `▸` volatile markers + Strip manual-recalc / `F9` re-roll shortcut. **Inspector:** Volatile fan-out timing + distribution stats probe. **Notebook:** Fan/histogram chart card + `[Re-run Simulation F9]` button. **Model Map:** `Sweep` director composite with inline percentile fan chart (`watershed.html`). **App:** Outcome probability band chart + risk KPI cards (`P10 / Median / P90`).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **10. Control panels** (`Stock!Slider_RP`, `Budget!Inputs!C2`, switches/flags): Human sees: Form Controls (sliders, checkboxes, dropdowns, spin buttons) or Data-Validation dropdown cells driving model flags (`Sim.Reset`, `ActiveScenario`). DNA Calc recognises: Native OOXML Form Controls / ActiveX controls with linked cells (**High 0.99**); DV list cells referenced by `IF`/`IFS`/`SWITCH` (**High 0.87**). Confirm/correct: Bind/unbind control range (`min`/`max`/`step`) or promote any DV cell to Parameter Rail. Views: **Classic:** Native interactive Excel Form Controls rendered on-sheet (`M-07`). **Inspector:** Lists all controls + linked cells + downstream impact count. **Notebook:** Inline interactive toggles/dropdowns embedded in narrative (`M-04`). **Model Map:** Docked right-hand **Parameter Rail** synchronized live with on-sheet control (`M-15`). **App:** Primary styled input widgets (`M-16`).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **11. Pivots** (`Sales!Report` PivotTable + slicers): Human sees: Dynamic cross-tab summary (`Row`/`Column`/`Values` headers, `Grand Total`, filter dropdowns) backed by a Table or data range. DNA Calc recognises: Native OOXML `PivotTableDefinition` + cache source (**High 1.00**). Confirm/correct: Inspect source binding, refresh cache (`Alt+F5`), or link reconciliation checks. Views: **Classic:** Full interactive PivotTable + field-list drawer + slicers. **Inspector:** Shows cache freshness (`Stale vs Fresh`), source row coverage (`25,000/25,000`), and `GETPIVOTDATA` dependents. **Notebook:** Clean read-only live Pivot card with filter chips. **Model Map:** Single aggregation actor `[Pivot: Sales by Region × Qtr]` wired from `Orders`. **App:** Interactive summary card with filter dropdowns (no raw field list).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **12. Live data** (`watershed` RTD Clock & Market feeds, `STOCKHISTORY`, async add-ins): Human sees: Streaming quotes/ticks (`=RTD(...)`), web/add-in feeds (`=TAX.EFFRATE(...)`), or `NOW()`/`TODAY()` cells updating externally. DNA Calc recognises: `RTD` / `CUBE*` / async UDF / `STOCKHISTORY` / `WEBSERVICE` AST nodes (**High 0.99**). Confirm/correct: Set UI visual throttle/pause rate (never alters formula); approve/inspect add-in trust. Views: **Classic:** `signal` (`#FF8001`) `▸` corner tick + hover freshness timestamp. **Inspector:** `Live & Volatile` monitor showing per-topic update rate, event log, and dirty-set size (`M-13`). **Notebook:** Live readout chip with subtle update pulse + timestamp caption. **Model Map:** `Events` director + `signal`-framed RTD source actors + top Event Queue strip (`watershed.html`). **App:** Live status badge (`Live · updated 1s ago`) + pause toggle.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **13. Macro-driven models** (`Inherited!modRollForward`, button-triggered roll-forwards): Human sees: `.xlsm`/`.xlsb` files with VBA modules, sheet buttons assigned to macros, or refresh/roll-forward workflows. DNA Calc recognises: Presence of `vbaProject.bin` or macro-assigned shapes/buttons (**High 1.00**). Confirm/correct: Explicitly inspect read-only VBA source and click `[Trust This Session]` or keep quarantined. Views: **Classic:** Non-modal Mast security bar (`Macros blocked · [Inspect Code] [Trust]`); buttons work once trusted. **Inspector:** Macro inventory card (module names, LOC, signature status, read-only code viewer). **Notebook:** Disabled/trusted macro action chip only if explicitly placed. **Model Map:** Shows quarantined/trusted macro node badge without claiming formula edges. **App:** Exposes author-whitelisted macro buttons *only* after explicit session trust; otherwise explains quarantine plainly.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **14. Reports & dashboards** (`Budget!Summary`, `Sales!Report`, `Inherited!Exec_Summary`): Human sees: Presentation-formatted top sheet with large totals, percentage margins, charts, print areas, and minimal raw data entry. DNA Calc recognises: High fan-in / zero fan-out sink sheet containing formatted summary tables, charts, or defined Print Area (**High 0.85**; **Medium 0.68** without charts/print area). Confirm/correct: Confirm as primary Executive Output sheet so Notebook/App auto-scaffolding prioritizes it. Views: **Classic:** Faithful author styling + Excel Print Preview parity. **Inspector:** Output tier of Workbook Atlas; traces every KPI back to assumptions. **Notebook:** Auto-scaffolded headline narrative + KPI summary section (`M-04`). **Model Map:** Right-most output sink composite + Plotter. **App:** Top KPI strip + primary visual dashboard (`M-16`).
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **15. Stocks, flows, feedback & delays** (`Stock.xlsx`, `names-in-motion.html`, `watershed.html`): Human sees: Accumulator state cells (`Stock⁻ + Inflow - Outflow`), shift-register delay arrays (`HSTACK(DROP(...))`), `IFS` operating modes (`Normal`/`Stockout`), and feedback loops. DNA Calc recognises: Self-referencing state formulas + shift-array delay patterns + `IFS`/`SWITCH` modal cells over state variables (**High 0.93** under iterative calc; **Medium 0.70** when unrolled across time columns). Confirm/correct: Confirm state vs flow vs modal role; toggle `Presented` (`Stock⁻`) vs raw Excel view; pick `Ticks`/`Iteration` director. Views: **Classic:** Backing cells/names + Form Controls + spill frames (`M-07`). **Inspector:** Cycle topology + per-tick state delta log. **Notebook:** Interactive policy brief with sliders + trajectory charts. **Model Map:** **Native signature view**—state boxes, `z⁻¹` delay loops, inline FSM badges, directors, live ripple, and Plotter (`M-06`, `M-15`). **App:** Policy simulator with sliders, mode badge, and live history chart.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **16. *(Added)* Reconciliations & check blocks** (`Sales!Report!D14`, balance-sheet checks): Human sees: Audit/check rows testing `=A-B`, `ABS(diff)<0.01`, or `"OK"/"ERROR"` banners verifying totals match across views or sheets. DNA Calc recognises: Formulas comparing two independent aggregation paths (`SUM`-vs-`GETPIVOTDATA`, `ABS(...)<ε`, `IF(...,"OK","ERR")`) or labeled `Check`/`Variance`/`Diff` (**High 0.86**; **Medium 0.65**). Confirm/correct: Confirm expected zero-tolerance rule or dismiss non-check variance rows. Views: **Classic:** Highlights failing checks in Provenance Overlay without overwriting CF. **Inspector:** Dedicated **Checks Instrument** (`11/12 Pass · 1 Fail: Report!D14 = -$118,420`) with one-click root trace. **Notebook:** Compact verified badge (`✓ All 12 model checks pass` / `⚠ 1 check failing`). **Model Map:** Check-monitor badge on sink composite. **App:** Subtle footer integrity pill (`Model checks verified`) or honest warning if a check fails!
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **17. *(Added)* Dynamic array / `SPILL` pipelines & `LAMBDA` libraries** (`Stock!Supply.Pipeline`, `Sales!Report!E8` `FILTER`): Human sees: Single anchor cell driving a dynamic output footprint (`FILTER`/`SORT`/`UNIQUE`/`SEQUENCE`/`HSTACK`/`SCAN`) and workbook-scoped `LAMBDA` named functions. DNA Calc recognises: Dynamic-array spill metadata from engine (**High 1.00**); `LAMBDA` AST root in Defined Names (**High 1.00**). Confirm/correct: Inspect spill bounds, edit anchor formula in Formula Explorer, or document `LAMBDA` parameter descriptions in `customXml`. Views: **Classic:** Crisp teal spill frame around active footprint + `#SPILL!` obstruction highlight showing exact blocking cell. **Inspector:** Treats whole spill as one atomic node (never 500 cell nodes); lists `LAMBDA` library + call sites. **Notebook:** Renders spill seamlessly as a live reactive Data Frame. **Model Map:** Single array-valued actor box (`{0, 400, 0}`); `LAMBDA` names appear as reusable actor classes. **App:** Binds directly to dynamic tables/charts that auto-resize cleanly without broken range bounds.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Pattern **18. *(Added)* External-link consolidation & staging hubs** (`Inherited` 3 missing workbooks, paste-special staging tabs): Human sees: Formulas referencing `[OtherBook.xlsx]Sheet!A1` or staging sheets full of pasted external values feeding regional consolidation tabs. DNA Calc recognises: External workbook reference AST nodes (`[n]Sheet!Ref`) (**High 1.00**); high-constant staging sheet with external-file naming/notes (**Medium 0.64**). Confirm/correct: Inspect/remap missing link targets or explicitly acknowledge cached-value snapshot mode. Views: **Classic:** `signal` (`#FF8001`) `▸` external corner ticks + hover showing exact external path & cached date; non-modal Mast/Triage link manager (`M-01`). **Inspector:** Top-tier External Links rail listing every external workbook, cell count, and broken-link blast radius (`M-02`). **Notebook:** Prominent footnote/badge (`Includes cached data from 3 external files`). **Model Map:** Left-edge `signal`-framed external boundary actors. **App:** Clear data-freshness header warning whenever any KPI depends on an unresolved external cache.
why: Complete 5-view pattern specification.

statement: Strand v0.1 adopts an 'instruments, not ornaments' philosophy: dark calm petrol chrome (#193F49), bright working paper (#FFFFFF), mist surround (#EDF1F2), and colour reserved strictly for semantic meaning paired with a label or shape.
why: Reserving colour for meaning and pairing it with text or shape keeps working surfaces calm and avoids relying on colour alone.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand defines darker ink variants for text legibility on light paper: Teal ink (#1B5F6B) for structure, Amber (#FFB301) for focus/pending, Green ink (#2E6E5B) for changed/verified values, Signal ink (#A35400) for external/volatile sources, and Red ink (#C12923) for errors.
why: Darker semantic inks preserve legibility while giving each status role a consistent visual identity.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Typography separates three voices — Recursive for UI (27/22/18/15.5/13.5/12.5/11 px scale), Source Serif 4 for reading prose, and Recursive Mono for formulas/source — with installed open/system fallbacks and zero external font downloads.
why: Distinct type voices aid scanning between UI chrome, narrative, and exact Excel source while working offline.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand fixes geometry radii (Cells 0, Chips 5, Cards 9, Panels 14), spacing steps (2, 4, 6, 10, 14, 22), and 120–160 ms settle motion that respects reduced-motion preferences.
why: Consistent radii, compact spacing, and restrained motion keep the working surface predictable and accessible.

statement: Normal steady state is silent, shown only by a quiet steady mark in the status bar; pending, stale, previous, error, missing-source, and delayed statuses appear only when relevant, and revision/snapshot prose never appears on working screens.
why: Keeping steady state quiet ensures genuine exceptions stand out immediately without visual clutter.

statement: Cells and controls distinguish Normal, Selected (pale fill), Active (dark outline + amber inner accent), Editing (caret), Point mode, Error, Spill anchor, Spill child, Stale, Pending, Negative, Conditional format, Hover (neutral surface), and Keyboard Focus (outer stroke distinct from active cell).
why: Making active cell, keyboard focus, hover, and data states visually distinct prevents ambiguity during navigation and editing.

statement: Stored workbook number formats (including red parenthesised negatives) and conditional formats are preserved as model content; UI states and theme restyling must not overwrite or confuse them with application attention colours.
why: Workbook formatting carries user-authored domain meaning that must stay faithful across themes and views.

statement: Review surfaces distinguish Model changes from Presentation changes with separate headings and concrete before/after diffs (explicitly stating when zero cells, formulas, or names change) within one consistent review pattern.
why: Users need clear visibility into whether an action mutates the Excel model or only presentation metadata before confirming.

statement: All workbook views share one consistent shell: command bands (File, Home, Insert, Formulas, Data, Review, View), command search (Alt+Q), source address box, formula bar, view picker, sheet tabs, zoom control, and status bar.
why: A shared shell preserves orientation, source visibility, and workbook navigation across every view.

statement: Every view inside an open workbook shares one model state, one selection, one clock (when present), and one Undo history; switching views changes presentation only and never copies values or creates a second model.
why: Eliminating duplicated state ensures edits, repairs, and Undo behave consistently across views.
evidence: README.md, W04, NC07, S08, S09, F02

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified ¶3; verification.html §What was checked ¶5
statement: All UI iconography and assets are self-contained original SVGs with zero CDN calls, external web-font downloads, or Microsoft artwork/styling.
why: Guarantees offline reliability, zero external network dependencies, and copyright cleanliness.

statement: Every screen supports 200% zoom reflow (stacking split panes vertically when needed), high-contrast mode, reduced-motion mode, labelled form controls, and visible two-stroke keyboard focus on buttons, fields, and ports.
why: Ensures accessibility is designed and inspectable across every view and exception variant.

statement: Every scene pairs a Normal/story state with an Exception variant and three to six callouts in a 1440×900 product frame, with Previous/Next arrow stepping disabled when focus is inside an interactive control.
why: Designing normal and exception states at equal fidelity prevents error and refusal paths from being an afterthought.

statement: In the computation notebook, every written Excel formula sits directly above its live evaluated output, followed by the next formula and result with prose between links; this vertical chain is the primary reading surface.
why: Showing written formula above live output delivers a Jupyter-like computation chain without hiding the Excel source.
evidence: NC01–NC07; Sales Analysis!A10# → J10# → M10# → Q10# → U10# → J2

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (callout 1), NC07 (callout 2, 3); verification.html §A function cell ¶4
statement: Author, Read, and Across are presentations of the exact same underlying cells and workbook names; switching layouts changes presentation only without copying values or creating scenarios, and Read layout still shows every formula above its output.
why: Separating layout from calculation prevents authoring and reading views from drifting out of sync.

statement: Data-frame outputs show a compact row preview window (e.g., 4 or 10 rows) while explicitly displaying full dimensions and evaluating FILTER, GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, SORTBY, and totals across all 25,000 source rows; paging the window never alters aggregates.
why: Prevents a compact display window from being mistaken for a sampled calculation.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01, NC06 (callout 4, UI); verification.html §The computation lives in cells and names ¶2
statement: The notebook's visible backing sheet (Sales!Analysis) puts inputs in B2:B6, scalars above row 10 (J2, J5), notes in column Y (Y10), and dynamic-array spills in separate column lanes starting at row 10 (A:G, J:K, M:N, Q:R, U:V) so downward spills do not collide.
why: Separate column lanes allow vertical notebook reading order while giving every Excel dynamic array room to grow downward.
evidence: NC01, NC06, verification.html; A10:G…, J10:K…, M10:N…, Q10:R…, U10:V…

statement: Each notebook output binds to a workbook defined name (e.g., =Analysis!$A$10#); clicking an output name allows renaming with workbook-name syntax validation, conflict rejection, and exact updates to downstream references while keeping the cell anchor fixed.
why: Keeps formulas readable by name while maintaining standard Excel worksheet anchors.
evidence: NC01, NC02; scopeOrders, byRegion, byMonth, rankedOrders, chartData, scopeTotal

statement: Clicking a workbook name inside a later formula or live prose navigates directly to its producing cell in the computation chain.
why: Lets readers trace dependencies through the notebook in one click.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (callout 3, UI); verification.html §A function cell ¶5
statement: PIVOTBY in the computation notebook produces a dynamic-array formula result (using explicit header/total arguments and keeping its month-heading row in the backing spill) rather than a PivotTable cache, and never invents extra months beyond source data.
why: Clarifies exact Excel PIVOTBY semantics and backing spill dimensions (e.g., 3×2 spill for 2 regions × 1 month 2026-11).

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (UI); verification.html §A chart has ordinary data sources
statement: Notebook charts are ordinary Excel chart objects (SalesByRegion) referencing dynamic workbook names (Chart.Region and Chart.Amount via INDEX+ROWS over the ranked spill) rather than an invented worksheet chart function.
why: Ensures charts remain standard native objects when opened in Excel.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC02 (callouts 2, 4, UI); verification.html §A function cell ¶4
statement: Editing a notebook formula inline offers Ctrl+Space completion and signature help (`FILTER(array, include, [if_empty])`), and complete supported expressions recalculate immediately with no Run button required.
why: Matches Excel's live recalculation model inside a notebook editor.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC02 (callouts 2, 4, exception); README.md §Computation notebook route ¶2
statement: An incomplete or unsupported formula draft replaces all dependent notebook displays with an explicit draft state so stale outputs never masquerade as current successes; Escape restores the committed expression.
why: Prevents misleading stale results from sitting underneath an unparseable or half-edited formula.

statement: Notebook filter controls (Region, Status, inclusive November date handles clamped to valid dates) bind directly to ordinary cells (Analysis!B2:B5); changes update all downstream tables, charts, and prose immediately with brief change marks and no Run button.
why: Keeps interactive parameter controls backed by standard Excel cells.
evidence: NC03; Paid = 20,853 rows / R23,440,150; South > East by R25

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (exception), NC03 (callout 4, exception), NC07 (exception); verification.html §Spill growth ¶2
statement: Omitting if_empty on FILTER produces Excel's #CALC! when zero rows match, and downstream cells use explicit IF(ISERROR($A$10),$A$10,...) guards to forward the error cleanly with no earlier successful outputs or chart remaining.
why: Maintains exact Excel error propagation and avoids leaving stale visuals next to an errored filter.
evidence: NC01, NC03, NC07 exception variants; verification.html [T10]

statement: A LET formula cell expands an inline live binding tree showing formula structure and current evaluated values of each binding (items, amounts, SUM(amounts)), explicitly labelled as expression structure rather than a runtime execution trace.
why: Makes nested LET formulas inspectable in place without claiming to record Excel's firing order.

statement: Live RTD cells in the notebook (`Report!E2 =RTD("DnaCalc.Price",,"LARK","last")` feeding `Analysis!J5`) share one stream with Inspector (I02) and Data frame (N01), clean up old observers on navigation, and reveal Report!E2 accurately.
why: Prevents duplicate or leaked RTD observers across views of the same workbook.

statement: Generating gallery previews or print snapshots must be pure and never consume or advance a live RTD price observation or clock tick.
why: Prevents passive UI rendering or printing from mutating live stream state.

statement: When a live RTD provider is unavailable, the notebook asserts no current price or dependent valuation while keeping historical order totals completely independent and unaffected.
why: Isolates live feed outages from historical workbook calculations and prevents stale valuations from appearing live.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC05 (callouts 2, 3, 4, UI, exception); verification.html §A function cell
statement: A notebook function cell defines a workbook-scoped defined name referring to a LAMBDA (`MarginPct =LAMBDA(revenue,cost,IF(revenue=0,0,(revenue-cost)/revenue))`) whose output displays a callable signature rather than a fabricated scalar from an uncalled worksheet cell, invoked by ordinary callers across any sheet.
why: Matches Excel's named-LAMBDA contract so reusable notebook functions work natively in Excel.

statement: Dynamic-array spill growth is a real model event: when a growing FILTER hits an obstructing formula cell (A16), A10 returns #SPILL! and explicit error guards forward #SPILL! to all dependents with zero partial output, prior chart, or successful-looking prose remaining.
why: Makes Excel's spill collision semantics honest and unmistakable in the notebook.
evidence: NC06; West+Pending A10:G10 vs All A10:G4156 blocked at A16

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC06 (callout 3, UI, exception); verification.html §Spill growth ¶2
statement: Reviewing a spill relocation moves only the obstructing formula and its defined name (e.g., reviewNote `="Review with Sam"`) to an empty cell (Y10 or Y12) without altering FILTER; Apply is disabled if the proposed destination is occupied, Cancel is inert, and Undo restores A16 and the #SPILL! blockage.
why: Repairs spill conflicts safely without overwriting user cells or altering the growing formula.
evidence: NC06; A16 → Y10 (or Y12 when Y10 occupied)

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC06 (callout 5, UI), NC01; verification.html §Corrections table row 3
statement: Opening Classic / Backing cells from the computation notebook shows the exact current live calculation state (preserving active criteria like Paid) with outlined worksheet anchors mapped directly to the adjacent notebook cells.
why: Demonstrates that the notebook and Classic grid are two views of the exact same live cells.

source: pro21/verification.html §The computation lives in cells and names ¶1
statement: Date values in proposed Analysis workbooks must be stored as real Excel date serial numbers in native files; ISO date strings are only an HTML prototype representation.
why: Ensures DATE() filter comparisons evaluate accurately in native Excel.

statement: The Sales computation notebook backs its chain with concrete Excel formulas using structured Table references, FILTER, IF(ISERROR(...)) guards, GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, SORTBY, LET, and RTD, preserving accepted user-edited formula text as written.
why: Grounds the computation notebook in exact verifiable Excel syntax rather than pseudo-code.

statement: Starting an empty Notebook while a cell is selected (e.g., Summary!B7) offers a concrete first step ('Add selected result') so authors build narratives directly around live workbook results.
why: Removes blank-page friction and anchors new notebooks to real worksheet cells from the start.

source: pro21/notebook.html F03 (callouts 1, 2, 4, UI, exception); storyboards.html S04 (callouts 1, 2, UI)
statement: A director-review Notebook embeds bound live numbers in narrative prose, workbook-owned charts, and cell-bound controls (slider, dropdown, Boolean checkbox), explicitly noting when an input (e.g., Debtor days Inputs!B12) does not affect an excerpt and keeping sibling valid cards visible when one card hits #SPILL!.
why: Combines executive narrative with live model exploration without detaching figures from their cells.
evidence: F03, S04; Budget Inputs!B3, B12, Summary!D2, B7, A20

source: pro21/notebook.html F03 (callout 3, UI); storyboards.html S05 (callout 3, UI)
statement: The Formula lens is a read-only presentation showing human-readable terms alongside the exact source formula (e.g., Revenue − Variable cost − Fixed cost beside =B8-B9-B10) without rewriting the source formula or adding workbook names.
why: Aids formula comprehension without silently mutating the underlying spreadsheet.

statement: Sorting or filtering a Notebook data frame over an Excel Table defaults to View-only presentation and leaves the Table's stored filter and row addresses untouched.
why: Prevents casual exploration from accidentally mutating shared Excel Tables.

statement: Choosing 'Changes the Table' on a Notebook data frame goes through explicit review and Apply to sort/filter the shared Table and update sheet row addresses (with Undo restoring row order and stored filters), while Find and Copy all matches always operate on the full matching scope.
why: Supports deliberate Table mutations with clear review and Undo alongside complete-scope search/copy.

statement: A live RTD price embedded in Notebook prose stays separate from historical Table rows, labels its last received value as 'stale' when the source is unavailable, and never revises historical order amounts.
why: Keeps live external feed staleness visible and isolated from immutable historical records.

statement: The horizontal Notebook pipeline lays out existing sheets left-to-right (Inputs → Monthly → Summary) as reading order without altering calculation order, labels windowed excerpts (3 of 12 months while the annual total sums all 12), and marks prior result cards 'Previous result' while an input change is pending.
why: Offers a cross-sheet flow overview while staying honest about calculation order, excerpt windows, and pending recalculation.

source: pro21/classic.html F01 (callouts 1, 2, 3, 4, UI, exception), C02 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI, exception)
statement: In Classic formula editing and Point mode, switching sheets to pick references keeps the original edit destination fixed (e.g., editing Monthly!B8 while picking Inputs!B3); references use coloured, numbered tokens and distinct border patterns, pending drafts never overwrite committed values, and Enter/Commit vs Escape preserve distinct commit/cancel semantics.
why: Matches Excel's cross-sheet reference picking while making references accessible without relying on colour alone.

statement: Pressing Alt displays discoverable key tips over compact original command controls (borrowing Excel's command access structure without copying Microsoft artwork), Escape dismisses key tips, and every command remains available via Alt+Q search.
why: Supports rapid keyboard-driven command invocation familiar to Excel users.

statement: F4 (and four matching anchor buttons) cycles a formula reference through relative, fully absolute, row-absolute, and column-absolute forms (B3 → $B$3 → B$3 → $B3), showing that anchoring changes copy adjustment without altering the current source value.
why: Delivers exact Excel F4 muscle memory with clear feedback.

statement: Dragging the fill handle shows a destination hatch and live preview of the adjusted destination formula (`=F8-F9-F10`), applies normal relative-reference copying on release, offers a visible Fill button alternative, and reverses in one Undo step.
why: Pairs familiar Excel fill gestures with live formula previews and keyboard/click accessibility.

statement: Ctrl+Enter writes one entry into all cells of a multi-cell selection while retaining the selection, offers a visible button alternative, reverses in one Undo step, and is never intercepted by shell or agent shortcuts.
why: Protects core Excel multi-cell entry muscle memory from shell or AI shortcut collisions.

statement: Dragging a cell's border previews the destination outline and moves the cell intact (e.g., Summary!A21 → D21 to unblock `=TRANSPOSE(Monthly!B11:M11)` at A20), Undo restores both the cell and `#SPILL!`, and spill children cannot be edited independently.
why: Supports standard Excel border-drag moves and lossless spill recovery.

statement: Alt+Q opens keyboard-navigable command search (filter, Up/Down, Enter, Escape returning focus to the active cell) inside dense workbooks, keeping missing external sources (Rates2024.xlsx) and disabled macros (LegacyClose) clearly separated from the selected local formula.
why: Lets analysts find and run commands without losing coordinate focus in dense spreadsheets.

statement: Opening a large workbook displays the last saved viewport immediately with stale values visibly labelled (never silently refreshing missing links), runs background reference inspection (e.g., 12/40 sheets) without blocking navigation, editing, or inspection, lists visible/hidden sheet counts in the outline, and surfaces recovery state.
why: Keeps large workbooks immediately usable on open while staying strictly honest about saved vs recalculated values.

statement: Classic verification preserves live model state from Model map (including unapplied repairs), supports native cell-bound form-control sliders (Stock!B5), shows explicit iteration settings (max 100, tolerance 0.001) without inventing an iteration count, and on a non-converging proposal (`B8=B8+1`) retains the current reserve without claiming an observed iteration stop.
why: Keeps grid verification synchronised with Model map and honest about iterative calculation limits.

statement: Ctrl+Z in a source view dispatches the actual owning model's Undo stack, while text input fields retain standard native text-editing keys.
why: Prevents Undo shortcuts from hitting the wrong owner or breaking standard text editing.

source: pro21/inspector.html F02 (callouts 1, 2, UI, exception); storyboards.html S06 (callouts 1, 2, UI)
statement: Inspector diagnoses valid-Excel-but-wrong-business-answer results by tracing full-scope contributions across all 25,000 rows and isolating specific outlier rows with both Table data row and worksheet row addresses.
why: Helps users uncover semantic spreadsheet errors that produce ordinary numbers instead of Excel error codes.
evidence: F02, S06; Sales Report!B5 128,450 vs 124,250; SO10482 data row 10482 / Orders!A10483:G10483

statement: When a PivotTable cross-check has an unrefreshed cache, Inspector labels it 'Stale cache' and refuses to treat its previous total as current confirmation until refreshed.
why: Prevents stale PivotTable caches from giving false confirmation during auditing.
evidence: S06, S07 exception variants; Pivot previous 124,250

statement: Inspecting a proposed one-formula repair previews exact before/after formula text, result delta, and changed-formula count separately from the current result until Apply; Undo restores the original formula, Cancel discards only a pending preview, and Close retains an accepted change.
why: Makes diagnostic repairs exact, reviewable, and cleanly reversible.
evidence: F02, S06, S07; Report!B5 adding Orders[Status],"Paid" (diff −4,200)

statement: Inspector traces a local #REF! directly to a broken defined-name formula (`Revenue.Window =OFFSET(Revenue!#REF!,0,0,12,1)`) separately from unrelated missing external workbooks, never presents stale cached values as the current formula result, and never guesses a replacement reference.
why: Isolates local name errors from external-link noise and prevents guesswork repairs.
evidence: S02; Inherited Summary!F18, cached 2,401,300 vs #REF!, Rates2024.xlsx

statement: Inspector's Copy evidence action preserves formula, name scope, error origin, and the stale-vs-current distinction, Reveal in Classic carries the exact selection across views, and protected sheets still allow inspection while requiring an authorised editable copy before repair.
why: Produces auditable diagnostic handoffs and respects worksheet protection without hiding evidence.

source: pro21/inspector.html F02 (callout 3), I01–I03 (callout 4); storyboards.html S02 (callout 2); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶5
statement: Dependency graphs, highlights, and wire animations are strictly dependency explanations and are never presented as recordings of Excel's execution order; any optional recorded order must be labelled 'DNA Calc's calculation order' and never invented.
why: Excel's dynamic calculation chain is implementation-defined, so claiming a dependency picture shows Excel's execution order is inaccurate.
evidence: F02, I01–I03, S02, F04, M02, O04, D03, verification.html

source: pro21/inspector.html I01 (callout 1, UI, exception), I02 (callout 1), I03 (callout 1)
statement: Live instruments keep observation capture controls (Record, Pause capture, Clear) strictly separate from the source's own Run/Pause controls; pausing capture leaves the source running and labels the chart as a recorded observation rather than a live result.
why: Lets analysts freeze and inspect recordings without interrupting or altering the live data source.

source: pro21/inspector.html I01 (callout 2, UI), I02 (callout 2), I03 (callout 2, UI)
statement: Minimum, maximum, and last statistics are computed strictly from the displayed observation recording, and Replay scrubs a cursor through recorded observations without writing to workbook inputs or replaying RTD events into the workbook.
why: Guarantees post-hoc analysis of recorded runs is side-effect-free.

statement: The RTD price instrument separately discloses source update rate, observation sampling rate, session received count, observed count, coalesced count, and last-received age (keeping the latest update per interval without claiming lossless capture), and retains the last received price labelled 'stale' with age when disconnected.
why: Prevents throttled or disconnected real-time feeds from appearing complete or falsely live.

source: pro21/inspector.html I03 (UI, exception); verification.html §What the controls mean ¶2
statement: In the ticked Live panel, Reset explicitly restores tick 0, stock 400, and an empty pipeline without erasing an existing observation recording (Clear is a separate action), and missing clock/guard evidence classifies self-referencing cells as Unknown.
why: Prevents simulation resets from accidentally wiping diagnostic recordings while enforcing honest cycle classification.

statement: Inspector organizes tools into four tabs — Precedents, Dependents, Calculation, and Live — alongside pinned signals, recorded runs, Copy evidence, and one-step Source navigation.
why: Groups diagnostic evidence and live instrumentation cleanly while keeping backing cells one step away.

source: pro21/model-map.html F04 (callout 3, exception), M01 (callout 3, exception), M02 (callout 3); S08 (callout 3); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶5
statement: Model map uses distinct visual structures and labels to separate period-row delays (`H15→C18`), per-tick state delays (`z⁻¹`), and within-calculation iterative circular references (Reserve enclosure); a circular reference without confirmed delay or iteration settings is labelled Unknown rather than inventing a mechanism.
why: A circular reference is not a delay; conflating period lags, clocked state, and iterative solving misrepresents model semantics.
evidence: F04, M01, M02, S08, D03, O04, verification.html

source: pro21/model-map.html F04 (callouts 1, 2, 4, UI), M01 (callouts 1, 4, UI), D03 (callout 3)
statement: Map nodes display live values on source-bound ports, support keyboard selection, provide a Source toggle for compact inline formulas and a grid button for backing cells, and expose a Connections list as a keyboard- and reduced-motion-accessible alternative to thin animated wires.
why: Keeps diagrams anchored to exact cells while ensuring full accessibility without mouse hovering or animation.

statement: Hierarchical map groups (e.g., Replenishment) open into member nodes and return through breadcrumbs (`Stock › Replenishment › Day 5`) without losing selection or shared parameter controls.
why: Supports layered systems-model navigation without duplicating sheets.

statement: Wiring a port to a specific operand on the Model map previews the exact before/after Excel formula and current-vs-preview value before Apply (leaving other order formulas intact); subsequent parameter edits recompute both sides of the preview, Cancel closes pending preview, Close keeps accepted changes, and protected targets permit preview inspection while blocking Apply.
